docs.title: PocketCW
docs.text:
PocketCW is open-source replacement firmware for the HamCube Morse code trainer. The Mini and the Pro run the same firmware, so PocketCW runs on both. The Pro adds a decoder board that listens to a radio. PocketCW is free software under the GPL-3.0-or-later license.

PocketCW is not affiliated with HamCube or Nintendo.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• An iambic keyer that also works with a straight key or a sideswiper, with a live decode of what you send.
  • A timing tape and histograms that show how close your keying is to standard timing.
  • Receive drills: Koch groups, common words, callsigns, and full ragchew QSOs to copy.
  • QSO practice: activate a park or a summit and work a pileup, or hunt activators.
  • Four memories that key your radio, with repeat for calling CQ.
  • Copy accuracy per character, your most common mixups, and practice history.
  • A USB keyboard mode that types what you key, or keys VBand.

PocketCW was tested on a Mini with board version 2.64. Other boards from 2.60 and the Pro may work, but nobody has tried them yet.

docs.title: The repository
docs.text:
Path What it holds firmware/ The pocketcw-firmware crate: drivers, the UI, and the RTIC app. It builds only for the device. logic/ The pocketcw-logic crate: everything that does not touch hardware. It builds and tests on your computer. tools/ Build, install and release scripts, and the font generator. docs/ This documentation.

PocketCW is licensed under the GPL-3.0-or-later. The fonts come from B612 Mono, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Rust from rustup, version 1.88 or later. The code uses let chains, from the 2024 edition.
  • The target for the AT32F403A, a Cortex-M4F:
rustup target add thumbv7em-none-eabihf
  • The LLVM tools. mkimage.sh takes llvm-objcopy and llvm-objdump from the rustup toolchain folder.
rustup component add llvm-tools
  • To flash from macOS: clang from the Xcode command line tools.

docs.title: Build the image
docs.text:
sh tools/mkimage.sh

The script builds firmware/ in release mode and writes firmware/target/A000014.bin. firmware/.cargo/config.toml sets the target, so a plain cargo build in firmware/ also builds for the device.

The script stops with an error in two cases:

  • The image does not start at 0x08005000. The bootloader is below that address. See Flash layout.
  • The image is larger than 236 KB, the app area.

At the end, the script prints the command that flashes the image.

The linker script firmware/memory.x puts the app at 0x08005000, with 236 KB of flash and 64 KB of RAM. firmware/build.rs passes the nmagic option to the linker. Without it, the linker maps the ELF headers at 0x08000000, inside the bootloader, and mkimage.sh refuses the image.

docs.title: Flash the image
docs.text:
The device installs updates through its bootloader, which shows a USB drive. macOS must not mount that drive. See Flash layout for the reason.

  1. Build the install tool once. mkimage.sh prints a command that runs it from tools/:
clang -O2 -arch arm64 -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=10.15 -o tools/pocketcw-flash tools/pocketcw-flash.c -framework DiskArbitration -framework CoreFoundation
  1. Run the command that mkimage.sh printed:
tools/pocketcw-flash firmware/target/A000014.bin
  1. Follow the steps the tool prints. macOS asks for your Mac login password, because the tool writes to the raw disk through authopen.

pocketcw-flash refuses a file that would write below 0x08005000, or past the end of the 256 KB flash. The install guide and troubleshooting pages cover the steps on the device.

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
The tests run on your computer:

cd logic
cargo test

logic/ has no target setting, so it builds for your computer. The firmware crate has no tests.

docs.title: Hardware probe
docs.text:
firmware/src/bin/probe.rs is a separate image for checking a board. It shows the chip and board IDs, scans the I2C bus, shows the live inputs, and tests the audio codec, the PA8 audio output and standby.

sh tools/mkimage.sh probe

The probe image also goes to firmware/target/A000014.bin. Flash it the same way, and flash the app again after.

docs.title: USB probe
docs.text:
firmware/src/bin/usbprobe.rs is a separate image for checking the USB device. It shows up on the computer as a USB keyboard named "PocketCW USB probe".

sh tools/mkimage.sh usbprobe
Input Sends Dit contact (tip) Holds Left Ctrl, as VBand reads a dit. Dah contact (ring) Holds Right Ctrl, as VBand reads a dah. F1 Types cq test de pocketcw and Enter. Hold the dial 1.5 s Turns the device off.

The screen shows the clock source, the USB state, the bus reset count, and the reports the computer took. CONFIGURED means the computer accepted the keyboard. macOS may open its Keyboard Setup Assistant the first time; close it.

The image goes to firmware/target/A000014.bin. Flash it the same way, and flash the app again after.

docs.title: Code layout
docs.text:
PocketCW is two Rust crates. Both are no_std.

Crate Path Builds for Holds pocketcw-logic logic/ Any target Keyer, decoders, drills, bots, sound synthesis, settings and records. No hardware access. pocketcw-firmware firmware/ thumbv7em-none-eabihf only Drivers, the screens, and the RTIC app in main.rs.

docs.title: Why two crates
docs.text:
Everything in logic/ runs with cargo test on your computer, with no device and no probe. The rules that decide what the device does live there: keying, decoding, scoring, the QSO and hunt bots, the battery gauge, and the byte layout of each EEPROM record. They are the parts most likely to have bugs that a test can catch.

firmware/ holds what cannot run on a computer: register access, interrupts, the screen, and the order of startup. It stays thin. It reads inputs, passes them to logic, and draws or outputs the result.

When you add code, put it in logic unless it needs a register, a pin or the screen.

docs.title: logic modules
docs.text: Module What it does keyboard USB keyboard output: the key for each decoded character, the typing queue, and the Ctrl keys for VBand. keyer The iambic and straight keyer, the key jack debounce and stuck contact rules, and the func jack output lines. decoder Decodes your own keying into characters. listen Decodes a keyed line at any speed from 5 to 60 WPM: straight key keying, and the decoder board's tone line. timing, decode_lines Grades marks and gaps, keeps keying statistics, and lays out decoded text in lines. morse, text The Morse table, prosigns, fixed size strings, and word wrap. player Sends text as Morse, with optional human timing errors. synth, volume Mixes the sidetone, up to four stations, band noise and fading into one signal. Maps volume levels to codec registers. drill, letters, ragchew Receive drills, Koch levels, letter statistics, and ragchew QSOs. qso, hunt The bots for activating and for hunting. progress Practice history, one slot per session. memories, settings The memories and the settings, with their EEPROM records. record The EEPROM record frame and its CRC. battery, panel, board The battery gauge, the choice of screen type, and the decoder board protocol. buttons, input, ticks, rng, math Button debounce and events, button actions, tick arithmetic, random numbers, and math helpers.

docs.title: firmware modules
docs.text: Module What it does main.rs The RTIC app: startup, the tasks, saving, and power off. pins Every pin number. See Pins. clock, gpio, power, fault Clock setup, pin setup, power hold and standby, and the fault screen. lcd, backlight, gfx, font, fonts, theme, boot The screen driver, drawing, fonts, styles and palettes, and the boot screen. audio, codec, es8388, wm8978 The PA8 audio output and the two audio codecs. i2c, eeprom, store The I2C bus, the EEPROM, and where each record lives. battery ADC readings of the battery and the supply. link The serial link to the decoder board. usb The USB device peripheral for stm32-usbd, and the USB keyboard. ui/ One file per screen, plus shared parts: exchange and transcript for the QSO screens, tape for the timing tape. text A re-export of the fixed size string type. bin/probe.rs, bin/usbprobe.rs Separate hardware and USB probe images. See Build and flash.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
main.rs is an RTIC 2 app. A higher priority interrupts a lower one.

Task Runs on Priority Work sample TMR1 overflow, 17,578 times a second while sound plays 4 The next audio sample. tick TMR3, every 1 ms 3 Key jack debounce, the keyer, the func jack and LED, the four players and the sidetone, both decoders, and button debounce. board_frame USART1 idle line 2 Parses a frame from the decoder board and answers it. usb_events USB interrupt, and a pend from tick 2 Answers the USB host and sends the next keyboard report. ui Async, software task 1 The boot screen, all drawing, settings changes, saves, battery polls, and power off.

tick and board_frame send messages to ui on a channel 64 messages deep. When the channel is full, a message is lost and the status line shows n INPUTS LOST.

Keying and audio never wait for the screen. A full redraw takes about 70 ms, so each event redraws only what it changed.

docs.title: Fonts
docs.text:
The screen text uses B612 Mono Regular, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The font file is tools/fontgen/B612Mono-Regular.ttf, and the license is firmware/src/B612-OFL.txt.

The firmware does not read the font file. tools/fontgen turns it into glyph tables in firmware/src/fonts.rs. Do not edit fonts.rs by hand: the next run of the tool replaces it.

docs.title: The two fonts
docs.text:
Font Cell Size Use SMALL 10 x 16 pixels 13 px Main text. 32 columns by 15 rows fill the 320 x 240 screen. TINY 7 x 12 pixels 10 px Labels, units and chart axes.

Each font holds the printable ASCII characters, from space to ~.

docs.title: Glyph format
docs.text:
firmware/src/font.rs defines Font:

  • width, height: the cell size. Every glyph has the same cell.
  • chars: the characters, sorted by byte value. Font::draw finds a glyph by binary search.
  • pixels: 4 bits of coverage per pixel, 0 to 15, high nibble first, width * height pixels per glyph.

Font::draw blends from the background color to the text color by coverage. A character that is not in the font draws as a solid cell, so the gap shows on the screen.

A prosign draws as its two letters under a bar. ui/mod.rs does this in draw_char, so the fonts need no prosign glyphs.

docs.title: Make the fonts again
docs.text:
cd tools/fontgen
cargo build -r
target/release/fontgen B612Mono-Regular.ttf ../../firmware/src/fonts.rs

fontgen is its own crate, with fontdue as its only dependency. It builds for your computer.

The sizes and cells are in SPECS in tools/fontgen/src/main.rs. When a glyph has visible pixels outside its cell, the tool prints how many and writes nothing. When you change a cell size, change CHAR_W, CHAR_H, TINY_W and TINY_H in firmware/src/gfx.rs too. Asserts there stop the build when the two do not match.

The hardware probe uses the FONT_6X10 font of embedded-graphics, not these fonts.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
A release is a git tag vX.Y.Z and a GitHub release with these files:

File Contents A000014.bin The firmware image. pocketcw-flash The macOS install tool, for Apple and Intel Macs. LICENSE The PocketCW license. B612-OFL.txt The license of the B612 Mono font. THIRD-PARTY.txt The MIT notice of every crate linked into the firmware.

The install script docs/install.sh downloads A000014.bin and pocketcw-flash from the newest release. The docs site serves the script, so a change to it goes live when it reaches main.

docs.title: The version number
docs.text:
The version comes from version in firmware/Cargo.toml. The firmware reads it at build time, and shows it on the SYSTEM screen in the FIRMWARE row and on the boot screen.

Both crates have the same version. firmware/Cargo.toml also names the version of its pocketcw-logic dependency.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Run these on a Mac. release.sh needs clang with the macOS frameworks.

  1. Set the new version in three places: version in firmware/Cargo.toml, version in logic/Cargo.toml, and the pocketcw-logic dependency in firmware/Cargo.toml.
  2. Build once, so the Cargo.lock files take the new version. Commit everything.
  3. Build the release:
sh tools/release.sh vX.Y.Z
  1. Tag the commit and push the tag:
git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z
  1. Make a GitHub release for the tag, and upload every file in dist/. With the GitHub CLI:
gh release create vX.Y.Z dist/*

docs.title: What release.sh does
docs.text:
1. Stops with an error when firmware/Cargo.toml does not hold the version you gave, or when the working tree has changes that are not committed. Then the files always match the tag.
  2. Runs tools/mkimage.sh and copies the image to dist/A000014.bin.
  3. Copies LICENSE and firmware/src/B612-OFL.txt to dist/.
  4. Builds dist/pocketcw-flash for Apple and Intel Macs, macOS 10.15 or later.
  5. Writes dist/THIRD-PARTY.txt with tools/notices.py.
  6. Lists dist/ and prints the tag and upload steps.

Git ignores dist/ and tools/pocketcw-flash.

docs.title: Hardware reference
docs.text:
These pages describe the HamCube as PocketCW uses it. The Mini and the Pro run the same firmware, and the Pro adds the decoder board. The facts about the hardware and the vendor firmware were found by static analysis and emulation of vendor firmware V5.03. Addresses such as 0x080185E0 point into the vendor app image, which starts at 0x08005000.

PocketCW was tested on a Mini with board version 2.64 only. No Pro has been checked.

docs.title: Markers
docs.text: Marker Meaning Confirmed on 2.64 Checked on a board 2.64 unit. Confirmed The vendor code shows it directly. Confirmed in code PocketCW does it, and the code shows it. Not checked on a board. Likely Inferred. Not checked on a board. Role unknown The firmware drives the pin, but what the pin does is not known.

docs.title: Signal path
docs.text:
PA8 makes the audio. It goes into input 1 of the audio codec, and the codec's analog bypass sends it to the speaker and the headphone jack. The speaker amplifier needs PB12 high.

  • The vendor sends a square wave on PA8 at the tone pitch, from TMR1 channel 1 PWM. Confirmed on 2.64.
  • PocketCW uses PA8 as a 1 bit DAC: a 281 kHz pulse train whose duty changes 17,578 times a second. The codec input and the headphones smooth the pulses into sine tones and noise. Confirmed on 2.64.

PocketCW timing (firmware/src/audio.rs): TMR1 counts 256 steps per pulse at 72 MHz, which is 281.25 kHz. The duty changes every 16 pulses. Between sounds the duty stays at half, the silent level, so a new sound does not pop, and the sample interrupt stops.

docs.title: Codecs
docs.text:
The board has one of two codecs on I2C2. PocketCW tries the ES8388 address first, then the WM8978 address, and uses the one that answers.

Codec I2C address Boards WM8978 0x1A Older boards. ES8388 0x10 Board 2.64, which has no device at 0x1A.

docs.title: WM8978
docs.text:
V5.03.13 uses the ALIENTEK WM8978 driver: register write at 0x0801BEE8, register cache at RAM 0x200000F0. Its setup at 0x08005F04 leaves these values:

Register Value Effect R0 0 Reset. R1 0x00B Bias on, VMID 5k. R2 0x000 Inputs and OUT1 off. R3 0x06C Output mixers and OUT2 on. R43 0x010 ROUT2 inverted, for the bridged speaker. R49 0x004 Speaker boost. R44 0x000 Nothing into the input PGAs. R47, R48 0x170 Line input into the boost stage at +6 dB. R50, R51 0x01E Bypass into the output mixers at +6 dB.

Then it drives PB12 high and sets the speaker volume, R54 and R55, from the vendor volume setting (0 to 63, and 0 writes the mute bit). R52 and R53, the OUT1 volume, are written at 0x080164D4, but R2 leaves OUT1 off.

PocketCW writes the same values (firmware/src/wm8978.rs). Its volume level 44 gives 61 in R54 and R55, which is +4 dB.

docs.title: ES8388
docs.text:
No published vendor firmware sets up the ES8388, so V5.03 and V5.03.13 are silent on board 2.64. Unpublished V5.03.15, shipped on some 2.64 units, has working sound. See Board variants.

PocketCW (firmware/src/es8388.rs) follows the bypass start-up in section 10.4 of the Everest ES8388 User Guide:

Step Register = value Effect 1 0x02 = 0xF3 State machines in reset, references down. 2 0x00 = 0x07 Reference on, VMID 5k. 3 0x01 = 0x40 Analog and bias generator on. 4 0x03 = 0x3F ADCs down, analog inputs on for the bypass. 5 0x04 = 0xFC DACs down; LOUT1, ROUT1, LOUT2 and ROUT2 on. 6 0x26 = 0x00 Mixer source: LIN1 and RIN1. 7 0x02 = 0xF0 References up. 8 Volume Registers 0x27 and 0x2A (input into the output mixers), and 0x2E to 0x31 (output volumes). 9 Wait 100 ms VMID charges. 10 0x00 = 0x05 VMID 50k for play.
  • Analog bypass from input 1 to the output mixers, with PB12 high, plays through the speaker. At 0 dB output volume it is very loud. Input 2 carries no tone.
  • OUT1 (LOUT1, ROUT1) drives the speaker, and OUT2 (LOUT2, ROUT2) the headphones.
  • A plug in the headphone jack cuts the speaker whatever the codec setup, so the jack switch is in the speaker path. The switch reaches no MCU input, so the firmware cannot tell which output is in use.

docs.title: Volume
docs.text: logic/src/volume.rs maps the VOLUME setting. Level 0 mutes. Levels 1 to 44 go from -60 dB to +4.5 dB in 1.5 dB steps. On the ES8388, the output stage cuts first, down to -45 dB. Below that, the mixer input cuts in 3 dB steps. A cut before the output stage raises the hiss relative to the tone.

docs.title: Speaker amplifier
docs.text:
PB12 enables the speaker amplifier.

  • The vendor sets it high during WM8978 init, and toggles it with the mute shortcut.
  • PocketCW holds it low until the codec setup ends, which on the ES8388 includes the VMID charge. Then it drives PB12 high while the volume is above 0. At volume 0 the amplifier is off, so the pulse train on the codec input cannot reach the speaker.

docs.title: Synthesis
docs.text:
logic/src/synth.rs mixes five voices into one signal: your sidetone and four players, so stations can overlap.

  • Key edges rise and fall over 5 ms on a raised cosine, so they do not click.
  • WAVE SQUARE sums the odd harmonics up to 31. At 17.6 kHz this reaches the Nyquist frequency for pitches down to 284 Hz. A lower pitch loses its top harmonics.
  • Band noise has a 500 Hz bandwidth, like a receiver CW filter. Its 10 levels are 2.5 dB apart, up to an RMS of 0.35.
  • Fading goes down to a tenth at the top level. Each player fades at its own rate, so stations fade apart.
  • When stations overlap, the gain drops so the sum stays at one voice's peak. The gain recovers over 0.5 s, like a receiver AGC. A limiter above 0.8 bends noise peaks down so the mix does not clip.

docs.title: The reading
docs.text: PA1 is ADC1 channel 1: the battery through a 2:1 divider, read against the 3.3 V supply. PocketCW also reads the internal 1.2 V reference on channel 17, which gives the supply voltage the ADC measures against. Each reading averages 8 samples at the longest sample time.

docs.title: Vendor behavior
docs.text:
V5.03.13 shows battery volts as counts times 0.0016169, for a 2500 mAh cell, and never reads a charge status. Confirmed.

Counts Volts Vendor icon 2037 3.29 1 segment 2345 3.79 2 segments 2400 3.88 3 segments 2470 3.99 4 segments below 1768 2.86 Shuts down

docs.title: PocketCW gauge
docs.text:
logic/src/battery.rs uses the vendor scale, but divider and regulator tolerances move the scale by a few percent on each unit. So the gauge learns each unit's reading at full charge and scales to it.

Rule Value Full cell 4.2 V, about 2597 counts at the vendor scale. Learned full point Within about 3 % of the design value. It takes a reading higher than the old full point, once 120 s have passed with no USB power, so charger surface charge has gone. Saved at 0x780. USB detect At startup, a reading 75 counts or more above the full point. Later, a jump of 60 counts or more up (USB in) or down (USB out) in one poll. With USB in, PA1 reads about 4.5 % above a full cell. Percent From a curve for a lithium cell under light load: 0 % at 3.4 V, 50 % near 3.82 V, 100 % at 4.2 V. Low Below 3.4 V, off USB. The status line says BATTERY LOW: PLUG IN USB, and the icon shows a red outline. Empty Below 3.2 V, or a supply below 3.1 V, for 10 polls in a row. The status line says BATTERY EMPTY: POWERING OFF, and 2 s later the device saves and powers off.

The UI polls the battery once a second.

When the regulator drops out, the supply falls with the battery, and a reading against the supply stays steady. A supply reading under 98 % of the highest seen marks a dropout. The gauge then scales the battery reading by the supply ratio. The ratio of two reference readings cancels the reference's own error.

None of the low and empty behavior has been checked on a board with a draining battery.

docs.title: Board variants
docs.text:
The board version is in option bytes Data0 and Data1. The vendor System Information screen shows it as (Data0 - 0xF0).(Data1 in hex): F2 60 is 2.60. The 2.64 unit reads Data1 = 0x64.

PocketCW was tested on board 2.64 only.

docs.title: What the vendor firmware reads
docs.text:
Vendor V5.03.13 runs on every board from 2.60. It reads the board version in three places only:

What Where Rule LCD init 0x08014F7A reads Data1 IPS init (0x080177E6) when Data1 == 0x63, ILI9341 init (0x080134F4) otherwise. Key output 0x08009F86, 0x0800A5E6 and 0x08013EE8 compare Data0 and Data1 with F2 60 PA3, the func jack ring, is driven only on 2.60. PA2 and the PB2 LED are driven on every board. System Information 0x0800C300 copies Data0 and Data1 to RAM 0x2000095C Display only.

V5.03.13 knows only the WM8978 codec. So a board with an ES8388, such as 2.64, is silent under it. A 2.64 unit shipped with unpublished V5.03.15 had working sound, so V5.03.15 sets up the ES8388. No dump of V5.03.15 exists yet.

Data1 does not reliably name the panel. The activation routine writes F2 60 on every board, so an activated IPS board can read 2.60.

docs.title: What PocketCW does
docs.text: What PocketCW Panel Asks the panel for its ID first, then uses Data1. F2 at power on overrides both. See Display. Codec Uses the codec that answers on I2C: 0x10 for the ES8388, 0x1A for the WM8978. See Audio. Func jack Drives PA2 and PA3 on every board. See Key and func jacks. System screen Shows the board version, the panel type, and where the panel choice came from.

docs.title: Known differences
docs.text: Part Older boards Board 2.63 Board 2.64 Panel ILI9341 compatible ST7789 style IPS ST7789 style IPS Codec WM8978 at 0x1A Not known ES8388 at 0x10

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
The device has four buttons, F1 to F4, and a dial that turns and clicks. See Pins for the pins.

Input Pin Level F1 to F4 PA4 to PA7 Active high, internal pull-down. Dial left, dial right PC14, PC15 Active high, internal pull-down. Dial click PA0 Active high. Also the standby wakeup pin.

The dial click also closes the dial left contact: PC14 reads high while PA0 is pressed.

docs.title: PocketCW timing
docs.text:
logic/src/buttons.rs reads every input once per millisecond, in the tick task.

Rule Value Debounce 8 ms. Press event Sent at the press, without waiting for release. Dial repeat While the dial stays turned: a repeat after 400 ms, then every 80 ms. Dial click hold 1500 ms, the vendor power off time. Release after the hold turns the device off. Dial left after a click Ignored while the click is down and for 50 ms after it opens.

The click that wakes the device is still down when the app starts. logic/src/input.rs ignores that click until it is released.

The F buttons also send a hold event after 800 ms, but no screen uses it.

docs.title: Panel override at power on
docs.text: F2 held at power on, for the first 50 ms that the app reads it, picks the other screen type. See Display.

docs.title: Decoder board
docs.text:
The Pro model adds a decoder board that listens to a radio's audio. The vendor V5.03 app image starts at 0x08005000. No Pro unit has been checked.

The host needs three things to use the board: power on PB13, the USART1 link, and the tone line on PB14.

docs.title: Power (PB13)
docs.text:
• Push-pull output (HAL_GPIO_Init at 0x0801560A and 0x08015618). Confirmed.
  • Driven low at boot, with PB2, PB7, PB12 and PB15 (0x08015598). Confirmed.
  • After the settings load, set from the "decoder board power" setting (0x08013244). The menu toggle near 0x08009F9E drives it high for ON and low for OFF. OFF also clears the board present flags. So high = board powered. Confirmed.

docs.title: Link (USART1)
docs.text:
• Setup at 0x08015858. 115200 baud, 8N1, TX and RX. PA9 TX is alternate function push-pull (0x080128C2), PA10 RX is an input (0x080128D2). Confirmed.
  • RX goes by DMA1 channel 5 into a 64 byte buffer. The idle line interrupt (0x08018C44) ends a frame, so frames need no terminator. Confirmed.
  • The frame parser is at 0x08005D00, called from 0x0801727C. Host frames end with \r\n. Confirmed.

docs.title: Board to host
docs.text:
Every frame starts with RE+ (string at 0x08022867), then a two letter code. Confirmed.

Frame Host action RE+IF1x Marks the board present and replies AT+OK\r\n. x = 1 sets a second flag whose use is unknown. RE+MD0, RE+MD1 Stores the digit. Use unknown. RE+FL0 to RE+FL2 Stores the filter setting. The vendor shows it as an icon. RE+NR0 to RE+NR6 Stores the noise reduction level. The vendor shows it as an icon. RE+MC, RE+AC, RE+MU, RE+VL Accepted, no action. Any other RE+ frame Replies AT+ERR\r\n.

PocketCW (logic/src/board.rs) follows the same rules. A known code with a digit out of range changes nothing. A frame without RE+ gets no reply, as in the vendor parser. Confirmed in code.

docs.title: Host to board
docs.text:
Sent through 0x0801D480, which formats and transmits. Confirmed.

Command When AT+FL<0..2> (0x0800BD7C) F2 on the decoder screen cycles the filter. AT+NR<0..6> (0x0800BD8C) F3 on the decoder screen cycles noise reduction. AT+VL<000..063> (0x080183BC, 0x0801B120) The host volume changed and the board is present. The value has three digits.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text: The host never asks. The board sends RE+IF1x, and the host answers AT+OK. Confirmed in code. That the board sends it at power up is Likely.

docs.title: Decoding
docs.text:
The board sends no characters. It raises PB14 while it hears a tone, and the host times and decodes the marks itself. Setup at 0x08006410 sets PB14 as an input with pull-down. The 1 ms SysTick polls it (0x080179CC calls 0x0800A094; high goes to 0x0801D6D4, low to 0x0801D71C). Confirmed.

The board manual describes no audio path from the board into the host, and the host gets no audio from it, only PB14.

docs.title: Vendor decoding rules
docs.text:
At 0x0801D6D4 and 0x0801D71C. Times are in 1 ms samples. Start values: unit 51, word 154, 20 WPM.

  • Up to 6 low samples inside a tone do not end it. A mark lasts the high run plus 6.
  • A mark under 0.5 unit is not an element. It pulls the unit down by a quarter of the difference, and a unit under 24 resets to 51.
  • A mark from 0.5 to under 1.5 units is a dot. A longer mark is a dash, and sets word = (word + mark) / 2, held to 77 to 365, WPM = 3850 / word, unit = word / 3.
  • A gap over 2 units ends the character. A gap over 1.5 words gives one word space. A 9th element clears the pattern.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
From the decoder board user manual and the Quick Start Guide. Confirmed in the manuals.

Port Use AUX1 Radio audio in, or the external MIC module. The board filters this and detects tone in it. AUX2 Stereo headphone or powered speaker out. AT+VL sets its volume from the host volume. AUX3 Not used. USB The Pro's charging port. No vendor code refers to it.

docs.title: PocketCW
docs.text:
All of this is confirmed in code and not on a board.

  • The DECODER BOARD setting, on the RECV tab, defaults to OFF, so a Mini sees no change. ON powers the board, starts USART1, and adds RADIO to the menu.
  • OFF stops USART1, sets PA9 as a pulled-down input so the board is not powered through it, and drives PB13 low. PA10 has a pull-up, so an idle line reads high with no board.
  • Frames are parsed in the USART1 interrupt and get the vendor replies at once.
  • The RADIO screen shows the board state, the filter and noise reduction (F2 and F3 send AT+FL and AT+NR), the heard speed, and the decoded text.
  • A volume change sends AT+VL once the board has announced itself. The value is the WM8978 speaker register for the same volume, 0 to 63.
  • PB14 is polled every 1 ms, only while the RADIO screen is open.
  • The baud rate comes from the crystal. The divider error is 0.16 %.
  • Frames with framing, noise or overrun errors count as ERR n on the RADIO screen.

docs.title: PocketCW decoding
docs.text:
logic/src/listen.rs decodes in its own way. The vendor rules cannot follow below about 10 WPM, count the bridged silence into every mark, and let a noise blip pull the speed down.

  • A dropout of 6 ms or less inside a mark is bridged, and the mark keeps its true length. A mark under 10 ms is noise.
  • Speed: two adjacent marks 2 to 4.5 times apart are a dot and a dash. The first pair sets the speed. A sample more than 1.5 times off the estimate replaces it, and other samples average in at 1/8. The range is 5 to 60 WPM.
  • The marks of a character are classified when the character ends, at the midpoint of the dot and dash estimates.
  • A character ends after 2 dots of silence. A word ends after 5 dots, or after 5/3 of the learned letter gap when that is longer, so Farnsworth spacing decodes. The letter gap is learned from adjacent gaps, the same way as the speed.
  • WPM = 1200 / dot length in ms.
  • Tests key known text and require it back: 5 to 60 WPM, 20 % jitter, dash ratios 2.5 and 3.5, Farnsworth 20/8 and 18/10, speed changes up to 3 times, pauses, dropouts, blips and noise bursts. The vendor test inputs are kept, with the sent text as the expected output.

The same decoder reads your keying in STRAIGHT mode.

docs.title: Display
docs.text: The LCD is 320 x 240 in landscape, RGB565 (COLMOD 0x55). It is on SPI1, which it shares with the SPI flash. See Pins.

docs.title: Two panel types
docs.text:
Panel Boards MADCTL Vendor init ILI9341 compatible Older boards 0xE8 0x080145E4 in V5.03, 0x080134F4 in V5.03.13 ST7789 style IPS Board 2.63 and later, 2.64 too 0xA0 0x080177E6 in V5.03.13

V5.03.13 sends the IPS init only when Data1 == 0x63, with a beq at 0x08014F80. So under V5.03.13, board 2.64 gets the ILI9341 init.

With the wrong init, the image turns 90 degrees and wraps into interlaced strips. The ILI9341 init sends C0h 0x23 (power control 1). On the ST7789, C0h is LCMCTRL, and 0x23 sets its XMV bit, which swaps the row and column address order. That gives the rotation and the strips.

firmware/src/lcd.rs holds both init sequences, from V5.03.13.

docs.title: Bus setup
docs.text:
• The vendor sets LCD CS, LCD DC, flash CS and LCD reset to large drive, and SPI SCK and MOSI to maximum drive. PocketCW does the same.
  • The vendor raises CS after every command and parameter byte. PocketCW does the same, but sends pixel data in one burst.
  • SPI1 runs at 18 MHz for both panels: APB2 / 4 in the vendor (HAL init at 0x08015ED8), APB2 / 2 in PocketCW.

docs.title: How PocketCW picks the panel
docs.text:
Data1 does not reliably name the panel. The vendor activation routine writes F2 60 on every board, so an activated IPS board can read 2.60 and get the ILI9341 init, under the vendor firmware and under PocketCW.

PocketCW picks the panel in this order (logic/src/panel.rs):

  1. A choice saved with F2 at power on.
  2. The panel's ID.
  3. Data1: IPS from 0x63 up, except 0xFF (an erased byte), which gets the ILI9341, as in the vendor firmware.

docs.title: ID read
docs.text:
After the reset pulse, PocketCW bit-bangs RDDID (0x04) and reads 32 bits on both PB4 and PB5. A panel answers on its SDO pin if one is wired, and on its bidirectional SDA pin otherwise. Each read runs twice, once with the pins pulled up and once pulled down. A pin whose 32 bits differ between the two reads is not driven.

The ST7789V answer 85 85 52, right after the one dummy clock that both datasheets document, picks IPS. An ILI9341 answers 00 80 00, or a module maker's ID with ID2 at 0x80 or more, so it cannot match. No ILI9341 ID is matched, because its D3h read is not documented for the serial interface.

The SYSTEM screen shows the raw 32 bits for each pin, or FLOAT. Not yet seen on a board.

docs.title: F2 override
docs.text:
Hold F2 while the board powers on, and PocketCW uses the other panel type. It saves the choice in its own EEPROM record at 0x7B0. Hold F2 at power on again to go back. A choice that matches the automatic one is saved as no choice.

The BOARD row of the SYSTEM screen shows where the choice came from:

Label Source ID The panel's ID. AUTO Data1. SET The saved choice. NOSAVE F2 was held, but the EEPROM write failed. The flip still applies until power off.

docs.title: Backlight
docs.text: PB8 drives the backlight from TMR4 channel 3, PWM at 20 kHz. PocketCW holds it off until the first screen clear, because the panel shows random pixels before that.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Region Contents MCU 0x08000000 to 0x08004FFF The vendor bootloader. Never write here. MCU 0x08005000 up The app. The app must set VTOR to 0x08005000. SPI flash 0x000000 Vendor boot screen, file F000000.bin. SPI flash 0x030000 Vendor UI images, file F0000C0.bin. SPI flash 0xE00000 Vendor fonts, file F003800.bin.

PocketCW uses only the MCU app area. It never reads the SPI flash.

firmware/memory.x gives the app 236 KB from 0x08005000, and cortex-m-rt sets VTOR from its set-vtor feature.

docs.title: Update files
docs.text: An update file name is a hex offset in KB, after a letter: A for MCU flash, F for SPI flash. A000014.bin is MCU flash plus 0x14 KB, which is 0x08005000.

docs.title: The bootloader
docs.text:
The bootloader is a modified Artery virtual_msc_iap demo. It shows a USB drive: "HAM MODULE" in the vendor manual, "POKEMON-2" on board 2.64.

To start it: hold F1 and F4, then hold the dial until the update screen shows. Plug in USB after that.

The bootloader routes file data by the name in the root directory entry. So the directory entry must reach the device before the data, as Windows writes it. macOS and mtools write the data first, and the data goes to the wrong place.

On macOS, PocketCW installs with tools/pocketcw-flash.c. The tool blocks the mount of the update drive, so macOS writes nothing to it. Then it writes the raw disk in the order the bootloader needs: directory entry, data, FAT, directory entry again.

After a finished write, the status file reads Success for about 1 second. Then the drive drops off USB and comes back as Ready.

A failed write leaves the bootloader in update mode at every power on, until a write finishes. The vendor upgrade notes say so, and a 2.64 unit did it. Likely cause on that unit: macOS mounted the drive when it came back Ready after Success, and wrote its own files to it. So the tool counts a write as done only when it reads Success, and it blocks the mount until the drive is back.

docs.title: Write protection
docs.text:
The vendor app has a one-time activation routine at 0x08018014, keyed to the chip UID. It writes these option bytes: Data0 and Data1 = F2 60, WRP0 = 0xE0, EOPB0 = 0xFE, Data3 and Data4 = D, y.

WRP0 = 0xE0 write-protects 0x08000000 to 0x08004FFF exactly. So on an activated unit, a flash write cannot overwrite the bootloader.

At every boot, the vendor app checks Data3 and Data4. If they do not hold D, y, the app overwrites itself with random data. PocketCW does not need these bytes. They matter only when the vendor firmware must run after an option byte erase.

docs.title: Key jack
docs.text:
The key jack, labeled "key", takes a paddle, a straight key or a sideswiper.

Contact Pin Level Tip PB1 Active low, internal pull-up. Ring PB0 Active low, internal pull-up.
  • The vendor default treats PB0 as dit. On the paddle of the 2.64 unit, PB0 is dah and PB1 is dit, so that unit needed the vendor swap setting. Confirmed on 2.64.
  • PocketCW with PADDLES NORMAL puts dits on the tip (PB1). STRAIGHT mode keys from either contact, so a sideswiper works. Confirmed in code.
  • In the vendor keyboard mode, the same pins carry the PS/2 clock and data, with EXTI0 on PB0. Confirmed.

PocketCW rules for each contact, in logic/src/keyer.rs. Confirmed in code.

Rule Value Why Debounce 8 ms Contacts bounce for up to about 6 to 10 ms. 8 ms is under half the 20 ms dot at 60 WPM. Closed at power on Does not key until it opens. A mono plug, or a key held at power on, does not key. Ring closed 5 s Stops keying until it opens. A mono plug shorts the ring. 5 s is longer than the longest character, 0 at 5 WPM. Tip closed 30 s Stops keying until it opens. Leaves time to hold a straight key down to tune a radio.

docs.title: Func jack
docs.text:
The func jack, labeled "func", keys a radio or an external keyer.

Contact Pin Level Tip PA2 High = closed. Ring PA3 High = closed.
  • The vendor drives PA2 on every board, and PA3 only on board 2.60. Confirmed.
  • PocketCW drives both on every board. With OUT TYPE STRAIGHT, one line follows the keyer output. With OUT TYPE PADDLE, the two lines follow the dit and dah contacts. OUT LINES swaps tip and ring. KEY OUT OFF holds both open. Confirmed in code.
  • A memory keys the func jack only with OUT TYPE STRAIGHT, because PADDLE output follows the contacts and not the keyer. Confirmed in code.

docs.title: LED
docs.text: PB2 drives the output LED, active high. The vendor lights it during every sent element, and the bootloader blinks it. PocketCW lights it while the keyer output or a memory keys. Confirmed on 2.64.

docs.title: The chip
docs.text:
• Artery AT32F403A, 48 pins, 256 KB flash. The flash size register at 0x1FFFF7E0 reads 256. The debug IDCODE is 0x70050242.
  • RAM is 96 KB for this part family. PocketCW uses 64 KB until the size is checked.
  • The 96 bit unique ID at 0x1FFFF7E8 shows on the SYSTEM screen.

docs.title: Option bytes
docs.text:
On the 2.64 unit, the low bytes from 0x1FFFF800 up read A5 FF F2 64 E0 FF FF FF FE FF 44 79.

  • FAP = 0xA5, so flash read protection is off. A running app or an SWD probe can read the bootloader.
  • Data0 and Data1 hold the board version. See Board variants.
  • WRP0 = 0xE0 write-protects the bootloader. See Flash layout and bootloader.

PocketCW reads Data1 at 0x1FFFF806.

docs.title: Clock
docs.text:
The board has an 8 MHz crystal (HEXT).

  • The vendor app runs the PLL from the crystal times 9, for 72 MHz (SystemClock_Config at 0x080185E0, HSE_VALUE 8 MHz at 0x08010E38). It hangs when the crystal does not start within 100 ms (0x0801861C). So every board that runs the vendor firmware has a working crystal.
  • The vendor firmware is built with Keil MDK on the ST STM32F1 HAL, with the medium density startup file and soft float. Its timer prescalers assume 72 MHz.
  • The clock source that the bootloader leaves running is not known.

PocketCW (firmware/src/clock.rs) also runs at 72 MHz.

  1. It switches to the internal 8 MHz clock (HICK) while it sets up the PLL.
  2. It starts the crystal, then runs the PLL from HEXT / 2 times 18. Each start has 100 ms.
  3. If the crystal or the PLL does not start, it runs the PLL from HICK / 2 times 18.
  4. If that fails too, it stays on HICK at 8 MHz.

APB1 and APB2 run at 36 MHz. Timers on these buses run at 72 MHz.

The CLOCK row of the SYSTEM screen reads the PLL source back from CFG.PLLRCS: XTAL, or HICK in red as a fault.

docs.title: Debug access
docs.text:
• The vendor app sets AFIO MAPR SWJ_CFG to 111 at 0x08011054. This likely turns SWD off while the vendor app runs, so a probe would need connect under reset.
  • PocketCW sets SWJ_CFG to 010: JTAG off, SWD on. This frees PA15, PB3 and PB4. It also remaps SPI1 to PB3, PB4 and PB5.

docs.title: Pins
docs.text:
firmware/src/pins.rs names every pin. The vendor firmware uses the same pins from board 2.60.

Pin Name in pins.rs Function Status PA0 POWER_BUTTON Dial click, the power button. Active high. The vendor sets PA0 as the standby wakeup pin before power off. PC14 also reads high while the dial is pressed. Confirmed on 2.64 PA1 BATTERY ADC1 channel 1: the battery through a 2:1 divider, read against the 3.3 V supply. See Battery. Confirmed PA2 KEY_OUT_TIP Func jack tip, keyed output, high = closed. Keys a radio's or keyer's dit input, or a straight key input. Confirmed on 2.64 PA3 KEY_OUT_RING Func jack ring, keyed output, high = closed. With PA2 it passes paddle contacts to an external keyer: dit on PA2, dah on PA3. The vendor drives PA3 only on board 2.60. Confirmed on 2.64 PA4, PA5, PA6, PA7 F_KEYS F1, F2, F3, F4. Active high, internal pull-down. Confirmed on 2.64 PA8 SIDETONE Audio, TMR1 channel 1. See Audio. Confirmed on 2.64 PA9, PA10 DECODER_TX, DECODER_RX USART1 TX and RX to the decoder board, DMA on RX. Confirmed PA11, PA12 none USB device. Confirmed (USB peripheral in use) PA15 LCD_RESET LCD reset. Confirmed PB0 RING Key jack ring. Active low, internal pull-up. See Key and func jacks. Confirmed on 2.64 PB1 TIP Key jack tip. Active low, internal pull-up. Confirmed on 2.64 PB2 LED Output LED, active high. Confirmed on 2.64 PB3, PB4, PB5 LCD_SCK, LCD_MISO, LCD_MOSI SPI1 SCK, MISO and MOSI, remapped. The LCD and the SPI flash share the bus. Confirmed PB6 LCD_CS LCD chip select. Confirmed PB7 LCD_DC LCD data or command, low = command. Confirmed PB8 BACKLIGHT LCD backlight, TMR4 channel 3 PWM at 20 kHz, duty 0 to 100. Confirmed PB9 FLASH_CS SPI flash chip select. Read command 0x03, 24 bit address. Confirmed PB10, PB11 I2C_SCL, I2C_SDA I2C2 SCL and SDA, to the EEPROM and the audio codec. PocketCW drives them in software at about 65 kHz. Confirmed PB12 SPEAKER_AMP Speaker amplifier enable. See Audio. Confirmed PB13 DECODER_POWER Decoder board power, high = on. See Decoder board. Confirmed in code PB14 DECODER_TONE Decoder board tone detect, high while the board hears a tone. Input, pull-down. Confirmed in code PB15 PB15 Output. The vendor drives it low at boot (0x08015598) and again after LCD init. PocketCW drives it low at boot. Role unknown PC13 POWER_HOLD Power hold, high = stay on. See Power. Confirmed on 2.64 PC14, PC15 DIAL_LEFT, DIAL_RIGHT Dial left and dial right. Active high, internal pull-down. Confirmed on 2.64

Without the pull-ups, the key jack inputs float and read at random.

docs.title: Power on
docs.text:
A dial click (PA0) powers the board up. PC13 is the power hold, high = stay on. Unless the app drives PC13 high, power drops about 1 s later, with the power-on reset flag set and the backup registers cleared. Confirmed on 2.64.

The vendor app sets PC13 high first at boot. PocketCW does the same in power::hold, right after the GPIO clocks start.

docs.title: Power off
docs.text:
The vendor long press, over 1.5 s on PA0, does this in order:

  1. Stops the backlight PWM and drives PB2 low.
  2. Saves the settings.
  3. Drives PC13 low.
  4. Sets the speaker volume and drives PB12 low.
  5. Enters standby: PWR clock on, standby flag cleared, PA0 wakeup pin on, wakeup flag cleared, PDDS and SLEEPDEEP set, WFI.

PocketCW (power::standby) waits until the dial click reads released for 8 ms, because the wakeup pin wakes the chip at once while PA0 is high. Then it drives the backlight, the speaker amplifier, the LED, both func jack lines and PC13 low, and enters standby the same way. Before WFI it disables and clears every interrupt in the NVIC, because an enabled pending interrupt ends WFI even with interrupts masked. If standby is refused, the chip resets.

Before standby, PocketCW saves the settings, the memories, the letter statistics and the current practice session. A failed save shows on the status line for 3 s.

docs.title: Wake
docs.text: A dial click wakes the chip through reset. The bootloader starts the app again, and the app must drive PC13 high to stay on. The standby flag always reads clear when the app starts, so the app cannot tell a wake from standby from a cold start.

docs.title: Fault screen
docs.text:
On a panic, a hard fault or an unexpected interrupt, firmware/src/fault.rs:

  1. Drives both func jack lines and the LED low, so a radio does not stay keyed.
  2. Stops the PA8 audio output.
  3. Shows the fault on a dark red screen: the file and line of a panic and its message, the PC, LR, CFSR, HFSR and BFAR values of a hard fault, or the number of an unexpected interrupt.
  4. Waits, with interrupts off, for a dial click, then enters standby.

docs.title: EEPROM
docs.text:
A 24C16 EEPROM sits on I2C2 at 0x50: 2 KB, as eight 256 byte blocks at addresses 0x50 to 0x57, with 16 byte pages.

The vendor firmware uses 0x000 to 0x367. PocketCW keeps its records above that (firmware/src/store.rs):

Address Record Magic 0x400 Letter statistics and Koch level Rl 0x480 Practice history: 32 slots of 12 bytes none 0x600 Memories Rm 0x700 Settings, copy 0 Rw 0x740 Settings, copy 1 Rw 0x780 Battery full point Rb 0x7A0 Boot count Rc 0x7B0 Panel choice Rp 0x7C0 up Free

Each record owns the bytes up to the next address, and startup reads all of them. So a longer record from later firmware still reads whole. Asserts in store.rs stop the build when a record grows into the next one.

docs.title: Record frame
docs.text:
logic/src/record.rs defines the frame:

Bytes Field 2 Magic 1 Version 1 Body length n Body 2 CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE of everything before it, high byte first

A reader takes the fields it knows from the front of the body. So later firmware can add fields at the end, and this firmware still reads the record. The version changes only when the body no longer starts the same way.

  • History slots are not frames. Each 12 byte slot ends in an 8 bit checksum.
  • Settings have two copies, saved in turn. Each copy ends its body with a save count, so a save cut off by power loss leaves the other copy to load.
  • The boot count record fits in one EEPROM page, so the write at every startup cannot tear it.
  • Records from before frames still read. Their magics are in capitals, and they end in an 8 bit checksum. A board that goes back to v0.1.0 after this firmware wrote its records sees blank records and uses defaults.

docs.title: Read failures
docs.text: When a read fails at startup, PocketCW starts with defaults for that record and refuses every write until the next power on. A write could otherwise replace a good record with defaults. The EEPROM row of the SYSTEM screen then shows FAIL.

docs.title: SPI flash
docs.text: The SPI flash holds 16 MB. The vendor resources end just under 0x1000000. See Flash layout and bootloader for what lives where. PocketCW never reads the SPI flash.

docs.title: No clock
docs.text: The board has no real-time clock. The date and time are lost at power off.

docs.title: Vendor firmware
docs.text: PocketCW does not include or need any vendor file. This page records what is known about the vendor firmware, for comparison and for going back to stock. See Go back to the stock firmware.

docs.title: Resource formats
docs.text:
• Images: an Image2Lcd header of 8 bytes (10 10, width as big endian 16 bits, height as big endian 16 bits, 01 1B), then RGB565 big endian, row major. This is the byte order the ILI9341 expects. Code refers to an image as 0xC0000000 | spi_flash_address.
  • Fonts (F003800.bin): starts with the text This is an image as font!, then a table of (width, height) byte pairs. Not decoded further. PocketCW uses its own font format. See Fonts.

docs.title: Why the vendor buttons feel slow
docs.text:
1. Buttons use the multi_button library with only single click and long press handlers. The tick runs every 11 ms. A click is reported about 110 ms after release. A second press inside that window becomes a double click, which has no handler, so the press is lost.
  2. The UI loops clear all key flags before and after each redraw, so a press during a redraw is lost.
  3. Images are read from SPI flash one byte at a time, without DMA, on the bus the LCD also uses. This makes redraws slow.

Paddle keying runs in the 1 ms SysTick interrupt, so the UI never delays it.

PocketCW sends a button event at the press, and reads buttons in its 1 ms tick. See Buttons.

docs.title: Vendor modes and settings
docs.text:
• Training: CW Memory, Code Listen, Koch Listen, Code Send, Followme, Chinese Code, Send Game, Listen Game.
  • Settings: F1 to F8 hotkey text, callsign, backlight, volume, decode lock and tolerance, auto shutdown, language, factory reset, date and time, key type (Auto, Hand, KeyB, Bug), Iambic A or B, dit and dah swap, tone, long and short code, decoder board power, Chinese decode, repeat group and interval, contact log (entry, view, ADIF export, init).

The vendor settings live at EEPROM 0x000 to 0x367. PocketCW never writes there, so the stock settings are still there after you go back. See Storage.
