docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
This manual uses these ham radio terms.

Term Meaning WPM Words per minute. The standard word is PARIS, so one dot lasts 1200 / WPM milliseconds. Dot, dash The short and the long element. A dash is 3 dots long. In this manual one dot length is also called one unit. Gap The silence between elements (1 unit), between characters (3 units) and between words (7 units). Koch method A way to learn: start with two characters at full speed, and add one character each time you copy 90 % of them right. Farnsworth timing Characters are sent at full speed, with longer gaps between characters and words, so the text arrives at a lower speed. QSO A radio contact between two stations. Over One station's turn to send in a QSO. Copy To receive Morse code and understand or write it down. CQ A general call: any station may answer. RST A signal report, such as 599. 5NN is 599 with the 9s sent as N. Prosign Two letters sent as one character, with no gap. This manual writes them in angle brackets, such as <AR>, <BK>, <KN> and <SK>. POTA, SOTA Parks on the Air and Summits on the Air: programs where an activator operates from a park or a summit and hunters contact the activator. P2P Park to park: a QSO between two activators. Pileup Several stations that call at the same time. Ragchew A long, chatty QSO. Fist How a person keys: their small timing errors. QRS, AGN, QRZ Please send slower; send again; who is calling me. TU, 73, 72 Thank you; best regards; best regards at low power (common in POTA). Sidetone The tone you hear while you key.

docs.title: Activate a park or summit
docs.text:
On this screen you are the activator on a park (POTA) or a summit (SOTA). You call CQ, a pileup of hunters answers, and you work the hunters one at a time. The device reads each over you send and answers the way hunters do on the air.

Open 04 POTA or 05 SOTA in the menu. The header shows QSO, the program and ACTIVATE.

Program QSOs for a valid activation You sign with POTA 10 72 SOTA 4 73

Set your callsign first on the CALL tab of the settings. The hunters listen for it.

docs.title: Work a QSO
docs.text:
Your over ends when you stop keying for three word gaps. The footer tells you what to send next.

  1. Call CQ: CQ POTA DE <your call> K. With an empty pileup, one to three hunters call you. Each hunter sends its callsign once or twice.
  2. Send the callsign of one hunter, then a report: K1ABC 5NN. That hunter sends your report and its state, such as RR TU 559 CA CA 72.
  3. Close the QSO: send TU, the hunter's state, and 72 or 73: TU CA 72 E E. The QSO goes in your log. Then the pileup calls again, and new hunters can join it.

The device counts a QSO as copied when your closing over holds the hunter's state.

More ways to talk to the hunters:

You send The hunters do this Part of a callsign, such as K1A?, or a callsign with one character wrong The hunter whose callsign matches best sends its callsign twice. A callsign after your closing, such as TU CA 72 K2XYZ 5NN You close one QSO and start the next. CQ, QRZ or QRZ? The pileup calls again. CQ without your callsign A hunter asks CALL?. QRS The last transmission again, 4 WPM slower. Each QRS slows the hunters by 4 WPM more, down to 8 WPM, until the QSO ends. AGN or ? The last transmission again. Anything else The hunter you work sends ?. With no hunter in a QSO, the pileup calls.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
The transcript shows each over: YOU for yours, PILE for the pileup, and the hunter's callsign for the hunter you work. What the hunters send shows as a row of dashes until the QSO is in your log, so you copy it by ear. F3 (HINT) shows the text.

Under the transcript:

Item What it shows NOW or LAST NOW during a QSO. LAST after a QSO: the items show the QSO you logged last. LOG QSOs in your log and the goal, such as LOG 3/10. The count turns green at the goal. COPY QSOs where you sent the hunter's state back. CALL The callsign of the hunter. A green edge marks a QSO in progress. RST The report the hunter gave you. During a QSO, only HINT shows it. STATE The hunter's state. During a QSO, only HINT shows it. After the QSO, the label is COPIED with a green edge, or MISSED with a red edge: whether you sent the state back. PILE How many hunters are in the pileup.

... marks an item with no value yet.

Under the items, your over shows as you key it. The footer shows the next step. With HINT on, the footer shows the exact text to send.

Band noise and fading play on this screen when you set them on the SOUND tab.

docs.title: Pileup settings
docs.text:
The QSO tab of the settings sets how the hunters behave:

Setting Values CHAR SPEED The hunters' base speed. MATCH uses your keyer speed. FARNSWORTH Longer gaps in what the hunters send. PILEUP OFF: one hunter at a time. TAKE TURNS: up to four hunters, who call one after another. OVERLAP: up to four hunters, who call at the same time. FIST HUMAN: each hunter keys with small timing errors. CLEAN: exact timing. SPEED SPREAD ON: each hunter sends up to 5 WPM faster or slower than the base speed.

Hunters send between 8 and 40 WPM. Each hunter sends at its own pitch, up to 200 Hz above or below your tone.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control Action F1 (SET) Stops the hunters and opens the settings at the QSO tab. F4 (BACK) there returns, and the hunters send their last transmission again at the new settings. F2 (QRS) The same as sending QRS. F3 (HINT) Shows or hides the hidden text and the exact next step. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu. The activation ends, and the log starts from zero next time. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Keys your over.

Each QSO in your log also counts in Progress.

docs.title: The controls
docs.text:
Control How you use it F1 to F4 The four buttons beside the screen, F1 at the top. Press a button to use it. The right edge of the screen shows what each button does on the current screen. A blank label means the button does nothing there. Dial turn Turn the dial left or right. Hold it turned to step again and again. Dial click Press the dial and let go within 1.5 seconds. Dial hold Press the dial and keep it down for 1.5 seconds. This turns the device off on every screen after the boot screen. Key The paddle, straight key or sideswiper in the key jack. See Keys and jacks.

Each screen page in this manual has a table of what these controls do on that screen.

On every screen, your key sounds the sidetone, keys the func jack when KEY OUT is ON, and types or keys VBand over USB when USB OUT is TEXT or VBAND. The Key row of each table lists what else the key does on that screen.

docs.title: Turn on
docs.text:
Click the dial. The boot screen shows Morse code falling as rain in the colors of your palette. The rain builds your callsign in large letters. Then a line with the version and your callsign shows, and a list of startup checks, each marked as passed or failed.

To skip the boot screen, press any F button or turn the dial. The KEYER screen opens after the boot screen.

docs.title: Turn off
docs.text:
Hold the dial. After 1.5 seconds the status line says RELEASE TO POWER OFF. Let go of the dial, and the device saves everything and turns off.

If a save fails, the status line names what was not saved, and the device waits 3 seconds before it turns off.

When the battery is empty, the device saves everything and turns off by itself. See System.

docs.title: The screen
docs.text:
• The header at the top names the screen. It also shows details such as the keyer mode or the speed, and a battery icon at the right end.
  • The column at the right edge shows the labels of F1 to F4.
  • The status line at the bottom shows short messages. A message stays until the screen draws that area again. See Status messages.

docs.title: What the device saves
docs.text:
The device keeps everything below when it is off. It has no clock, so it does not keep the date or time.

What When it saves Settings 2 seconds after your last change. Memories When you leave the settings screen. Letter statistics and Koch level When you leave a receive drill or a ragchew. Progress of this session At most once a minute. Battery calibration When it changes. Settings, memories, letter statistics and progress When you turn the device off.

If the device loses power in another way, such as when you take the battery out, it can lose changes it did not save yet.

docs.title: Hunt
docs.text:
On this screen you are the hunter. An activator calls CQ from a park (POTA) or a summit (SOTA), you work the activator, and then you log the QSO. About two activators in three are on a park. An activator on a summit signs with /P after the callsign.

Open 06 HUNT in the menu. The header shows HUNT and your callsign. Set your callsign first on the CALL tab of the settings.

docs.title: Work a QSO
docs.text:
Your over ends when you stop keying for three word gaps. The footer tells you what to send next.

  1. The activator calls CQ, such as CQ POTA DE K1ABC K1ABC K. While you are quiet, the activator calls again 3.5 seconds after each CQ. When you start to key, the CQs stop.
  2. Send your callsign. For a park to park QSO (P2P), send P2P with your callsign. The activator sends your callsign, your report and its state, such as K5XYZ TU 5NN CA CA <BK>.
  3. Close the QSO: send TU, a report, your state and 72 or 73, such as TU 5NN TX 72. The activator says goodbye: TU 72 E E.
  4. Log the QSO: key the activator's callsign, without /P. The activator you logged shows in the items, and the next activator calls 1.5 seconds later.

The activator can copy your callsign wrong. This happens when you send a callsign with one character different from yours. The activator then sends that wrong callsign in its exchange. Send your callsign again before you close, and the activator sends the exchange again with your callsign. If you close with the wrong callsign, the QSO is busted.

More ways to talk to the activator:

You send The activator does this Part of your callsign, or any word with a digit, before the exchange Asks for it again, such as K5?. Anything else before the exchange QRZ? Your callsign, during the exchange Sends the exchange again with your callsign. Anything that does not close, during the exchange AGN? QRS The last transmission again, 4 WPM slower. Each QRS slows the activator by 4 WPM more, down to 8 WPM, until you log the QSO. AGN, AGN? or ? The last transmission again.

A closing over holds TU, 72, 73, 5NN, 599, TNX or RR.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
The transcript shows each over: YOU for yours, THEM for the activator. What the activator sends shows as a row of dashes until you log the QSO, so you copy it by ear. F3 (HINT) shows the text.

Under the transcript:

Item What it shows NOW or LAST NOW during a QSO. LAST after you log a QSO: the items show the QSO you logged last until the next activator answers you. HUNTED QSOs you logged. GOOD QSOs where you logged the activator's callsign right and the activator copied your callsign right. CALL The activator's callsign. After you log, the label says COPIED with a green edge, MISSED with a red edge when you keyed a wrong callsign, or BUSTED with a red edge when the activator copied your callsign wrong. RST The report the activator gave you. STATE The activator's state. FROM PARK, SUMMIT, or P2P for a park to park QSO.

During a QSO, only HINT shows the values of the items. ... marks an item with no value.

Under the items, your over shows as you key it. The footer shows the next step. With HINT on, the footer shows the exact text to send.

Band noise and fading play on this screen when you set them on the SOUND tab.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: The hunt uses the QSO tab of the settings: CHAR SPEED, FARNSWORTH, FIST and SPEED SPREAD. PILEUP does not apply, because one activator calls at a time. The activator sends between 8 and 40 WPM, at a pitch up to 200 Hz above or below your tone.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control Action F1 (SET) Stops the activator and opens the settings at the QSO tab. F4 (BACK) there returns. The activator calls CQ again, or during a QSO sends its last transmission again, at the new settings. F2 (QRS) The same as sending QRS. F3 (HINT) Shows or hides the hidden text and the exact next step. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu. The hunt ends, and the counts start from zero next time. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Keys your over.

Each QSO you log also counts in Progress.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
This page installs PocketCW on a HamCube. On Windows and Linux, you copy one file to the device. On macOS, an install script does the copy, because macOS writes its own files to the device, and those files break the install.

PocketCW was tested on a Mini with board version 2.64. Other board versions and the Pro may work, but nobody has tried them yet.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A computer with Windows, Linux, or macOS 10.15 or later on an Intel or Apple chip.
  • A USB cable that carries data. Some cables only charge. If the computer never finds the device, try a different cable.
  • About 5 minutes.

docs.title: Is it safe?
docs.text:
The device has a small built-in program, the bootloader, that installs firmware. This install never touches the bootloader: the PocketCW file installs after it, and the macOS install tool refuses any file that would write over it. If an install goes wrong, the bootloader still works, and you can run the install again.

To go back to the original firmware, see Go back to the stock firmware. That page installs the published stock version, V5.03. Some devices come from the factory with a newer, unpublished version, and the install replaces it for good. On board 2.64, V5.03 has no sound.

docs.title: Update mode
docs.text:
The device takes new firmware in update mode. To start update mode:

  1. Turn the device off, and unplug its USB cable. To turn it off, hold the dial down for about 2 seconds.
  2. Find F1 and F4. They are two of the four buttons beside the screen: F1 is the top one, and F4 is the bottom one.
  3. Hold F1 and F4 down.
  4. While you hold them, hold the dial down too.
  5. When the firmware update screen shows, let go of all three.

In update mode, the device shows up on the computer as a drive named POKEMON-2 or HAM MODULE. The drive holds one file, READY.TXT.

docs.title: Windows and Linux
docs.text:
Nobody has tested a Linux install yet. The bootloader needs the file's name to reach the drive before the file's data. Windows writes the name first. If a Linux install does not work, report it on the issue tracker.

  1. Download A000014.bin from the newest release.
  2. Put the device in update mode.
  3. Plug the USB cable into the device and the computer. The drive opens.
  4. Copy A000014.bin to the drive. On Linux, run sync after the copy, so the file goes to the device at once.
  5. Wait about 10 seconds. The drive closes, then opens again with only READY.TXT.
  6. Unplug the device, then click the dial to turn it on.

If the drive holds a file other than READY.TXT before the copy, hold F4 to reset the drive.

docs.title: Start the script
docs.text:
1. Turn the device off, and unplug its USB cable.
  2. Open Terminal. Press Command and Space together, type Terminal, and press Return.
  3. Copy this line, paste it into the Terminal window, and press Return:
curl -fsSL https://kvmet.github.io/k5mme_pocketcw/install.sh | sh

The script downloads the newest PocketCW release and the install tool, then says "Waiting for the device".

docs.title: Plug in the device
docs.text:
1. Put the device in update mode. If it already shows the firmware update screen, go to the next step.
  2. Plug the USB cable into the device and the Mac. After a few seconds, the script says "Found the device".
  3. macOS asks for your password. Type your Mac login password, and click OK. The install writes directly to the device, and macOS asks for your password before it allows that.

docs.title: Finish
docs.text:
After about 10 seconds, the script shows this when the install works:

Finished. Unplug the device.
Then click the dial to turn it on.

Unplug the device, then click the dial to turn it on.

docs.title: While the install runs
docs.text:
• Do not unplug the device until the script says "Finished".
  • When the script finds a problem, it prints Problem: and the reason, then waits. Fix the cause, press Return, and follow the steps it prints again.
  • macOS can show a message about a disk it cannot read. Click Ignore. If you click Initialize by mistake, close the Disk Utility window that opens, and change nothing.
  • To stop the script at any time, press Control and C together.

docs.title: Check the version
docs.text:
On the KEYER screen, press F4 (MENU). Turn the dial to SYSTEM, and click the dial. The FIRMWARE row shows the version, such as v0.3.0.

If something goes wrong, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Release files
docs.text:
Each release has these files:

File What it is A000014.bin The firmware. pocketcw-flash The macOS install tool that the script runs. LICENSE The PocketCW license, GPL-3.0-or-later. B612-OFL.txt The license of the B612 Mono font. THIRD-PARTY.txt The licenses of the code libraries in the firmware.

docs.title: Keyer
docs.text: The KEYER screen is the main screen. It opens after the boot screen. The header shows KEYER and the keyer mode.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
Area What it shows Large digits Your sending speed in WPM, 5 to 60. TONE The sidetone pitch in Hz. VOL The volume, 0 to 44. 0 is off. OUT KEY OUT: ON when the func jack keys, OFF when it does not. DIT The length of one dot at your speed, in milliseconds. Bar Your speed between 5 and 60 WPM. Timing tape Your keying drawn to scale. See below. Statistics line Your average gaps and speed. See below. Decode Five lines of what your keying decodes to.

A small mark under a value shows which value the dial sets: speed, tone or volume.

docs.title: Timing tape
docs.text:
The tape draws time from left to right, 4 pixels per dot length.

  • The KEY row shows the keyer output. In STRAIGHT mode, each mark has the color and shape of its timing grade.
  • The two rows under it show the two contacts of your key: DIT and DAH, or TIP and RNG in STRAIGHT mode.
  • Under the rows, each decoded character shows under its marks.
  • Each gap between characters or words shows its length in units, in the color of its grade. A thin tick shows where the ideal gap would end.

A new page starts after a pause of 14 units or more, or when the next element would not fit.

docs.title: Timing grades
docs.text:
Every mark and gap gets a grade:

Grade Color Meaning Good Green Within 20 % of the ideal length. Off Amber Between good and bad. Bad Red More than halfway from the ideal length to the length where the decoder reads it as another kind, such as a dot read as a dash.

Each grade also has its own shape, so you can read the grades without color.

docs.title: Statistics line
docs.text: CHR and WRD are your average character gap and word gap in units (ideal: 3 and 7). RATIO is your average dash length over your average dot length (ideal: 3). The last value is the speed your timing works out to. Dashes in place of a value mean no data yet. F2 (CLR) on the Timing screen clears these statistics.

docs.title: Decode
docs.text: Each character has an underline in its grade: a thin line for good, a dashed line for off, a thick bar for bad. The grade is the worst timing in the character: its marks, its gaps, and the gap before it. * is a pattern that is not a character. A prosign shows as its two letters under a bar.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the KEYER tab. F2 (MEM) Opens the memory row. See Memories. F3 (OUT) Turns KEY OUT on or off. F4 (MENU) Opens the menu. Dial turn Changes the marked value: speed, tone or volume. Dial click Moves the mark to the next value: speed, then tone, then volume. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Draws on the timing tape and decodes. Stops a memory that is sending.

docs.title: Keys and jacks
docs.text:
The device has two jacks for Morse. The key jack, labeled "key", takes your paddle or key. The func jack, labeled "func", keys a radio or an external keyer.

The USB port can also send your keying to a computer, as typed text or for VBand. See USB keyboard.

docs.title: Key types
docs.text:
Set the key type with MODE on the KEYER tab of the settings. See Settings.

MODE Key How it keys IAMBIC A Dual-lever paddle One lever sends dots, the other dashes. Squeeze both levers and the keyer alternates dots and dashes. When you let go of both levers, the keyer stops after the element it is sending. IAMBIC B Dual-lever paddle The same as IAMBIC A, but when you let go of both levers after a squeeze, the keyer still sends the one element the squeeze asked for. This is the default. STRAIGHT Straight key The key closes the tip contact, and you time every element yourself. STRAIGHT Sideswiper Either side closes a contact, and either contact keys. You time every element yourself.

In both iambic modes, the keyer remembers a lever you press while it sends an element of the other kind, and sends that element next.

In the iambic modes, PADDLES sets which lever sends dots: NORMAL puts dots on the tip contact, and REVERSED puts dots on the ring contact. STRAIGHT mode ignores PADDLES.

docs.title: How the device reads your sending
docs.text:
• In the iambic modes, the keyer times every element at your set speed, so the decoder reads your sending at that speed.
  • In STRAIGHT mode, the decoder starts at your set speed and then follows the speed you actually send.

docs.title: The key jack
docs.text:
The key jack has two contacts, tip and ring.

  • A contact that is closed when you turn the device on does not key until it opens.
  • A ring contact closed for 5 seconds stops keying until it opens.
  • A tip contact closed for 30 seconds stops keying until it opens. This leaves time to hold a straight key down to tune a radio.

When a contact stops keying, the status line shows a message such as DAH STUCK ON: CHECK PLUG. In STRAIGHT mode the message names TIP or RNG (ring) instead of DIT or DAH.

A mono plug connects the ring contact all the time. Plug a mono plug in before you turn the device on: then the ring never keys, and the tip keys normally. If you plug a mono plug in while the device is on, the ring keys for 5 seconds before it stops.

docs.title: The func jack
docs.text:
The func jack keys a radio. It follows these settings on the KEYER tab:

Setting Value What the func jack does KEY OUT ON The func jack keys, on every screen. This is the default. KEY OUT OFF The func jack never closes. OUT TYPE STRAIGHT One line closes while the keyer sends, for a radio's straight key input. OUT LINES picks TIP KEYS or RING KEYS. OUT TYPE PADDLE Tip and ring follow your dot contact and your dash contact, for the radio's own keyer. OUT LINES picks DIT ON TIP or DIT ON RING.

F3 (OUT) on the KEYER screen turns KEY OUT on and off.

Only your own keying and your memories key the func jack. The stations of the practice screens never key it. Memories key the func jack only when KEY OUT is ON and OUT TYPE is STRAIGHT.

The LED lights while the keyer sends and while a memory sends.

docs.title: Letters
docs.text:
The LETTERS screen shows how well you copy each of the 44 Koch characters, and the characters you mix up most. The header shows LETTERS and your Koch level, such as KOCH 12.

Open 07 LETTERS in the menu, or press F2 (LTRS) on the Progress screen.

docs.title: Where the numbers come from
docs.text:
Every character you copy in a receive drill or answer in a ragchew quiz counts. A character counts as right, as wrong (copied as another character), or as missed.

When a character reaches 200 tries, its counts halve. The numbers then follow how you copy now, more than how you copied long ago.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
Each character has a tile, in the Koch order. A tile shows the character and the percent you copied right. The color of the tile shows how sure the device is that you know the character:

Color Meaning Green Known: the device is 95 % sure that you copy it at least 90 % right. Amber Not enough tries to tell. Red Weak: the device is 95 % sure that you copy it less than 90 % right. Gray, no percent Not sent yet.

Under the tiles, MIXUPS lists the six most common mixups, such as S/H 4X: the device sent S, you copied H, and this happened 4 times. Before your first mixup, the list says NONE YET: RUN A RECEIVE DRILL.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the RECV tab. F4 (BACK) there returns to this screen. F2 (CLR) Press once: the status line says CLR AGAIN TO ERASE STATS. Press again to erase all counts and mixups. Your Koch level stays. Any other control cancels the erase. F3 (DRIL) Starts the KOCH drill. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Memories
docs.text:
The device stores four messages, M1 to M4. You key each message in once on the MEM tab of the settings. Then you send it with one press from the KEYER screen. A memory can repeat, for calling CQ until a station answers.

The first time PocketCW starts, the memories hold messages for a POTA activation with your callsign:

Memory Message M1 CQ POTA DE <your call> <your call> K, set to repeat M2 UR 5NN 5NN <BK> M3 TU 72 E E M4 QRZ DE <your call> K

docs.title: Send a memory
docs.text:
1. On the KEYER screen, press F2 (MEM). The memory row replaces the decode lines and shows each memory. A lit label marks a memory that repeats. The labels of F1 to F4 change to M1 to M4.
  2. Press F1 to F4 to send M1 to M4. An empty memory sends nothing, and the status line shows M1 IS EMPTY (SETTINGS, MEM).

The memory sends at your keyer speed and tone. The status line shows SENDING M1 KEY TO STOP. A repeating memory waits for the REPEAT EVERY time after it ends, then sends again. The status line then shows the time to the next send, such as M1 AGAIN IN 6S KEY TO STOP.

A memory keys the func jack only when KEY OUT is ON and OUT TYPE is STRAIGHT. With OUT TYPE PADDLE, the memory plays only as a tone, and the status line says M1 TONE ONLY: OUT IS PADDLE.

docs.title: Stop a memory
docs.text: Touch your key, or leave the KEYER screen. While the memory row is closed, any F button or a dial click also stops the memory. A dial turn does not stop it.

docs.title: Controls with the memory row open
docs.text: Control Action F1 to F4 (M1 to M4) Sends that memory, in place of a memory that is sending. With AFTER SEND set to CLOSE, the memory row closes. Dial turn Changes the marked value on the KEYER screen. Dial click Closes the memory row. While a memory sends, the click stops it instead. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Stops a memory that is sending. With AFTER SEND set to CLOSE, the memory row closes.

docs.title: Edit the memories
docs.text:
Open the settings, and press F1 (TAB) until the MEM tab shows. The tab has six rows: M1 to M4, REPEAT EVERY and AFTER SEND.

Row Values M1 to M4 The message, up to 48 characters. A prosign such as <AR> takes 4. RPT marks a memory that repeats. REPEAT EVERY The silence between two sends of a repeating memory: 2 to 30 seconds. The default is 6 seconds. AFTER SEND CLOSE closes the memory row after a send. STAY OPEN keeps the memory row open, for one QSO after another.

A hint line under the rows tells you how to use the selected row. On a memory row, it shows how many characters are left.

docs.title: Controls on a memory row
docs.text: Control Action F1 (TAB) Opens the next tab. F2 (DEL) Deletes the last character. A prosign goes as one character. F3 (CLR) Clears the memory. F4 (BACK) Leaves the settings. Dial turn Selects another row. Dial click Turns repeat on or off for this memory. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Adds what you key to the memory. A prosign goes in as <AR>. The memory gets one space between words, and no space at the start. When the memory is full, the status line shows MEMORY FULL.

docs.title: Controls on REPEAT EVERY and AFTER SEND
docs.text:
Control Action F1 (TAB) Opens the next tab. F2 (-), F3 (+) REPEAT EVERY: one second less or more. AFTER SEND: changes the value. F4 (BACK) Leaves the settings. Dial turn Selects another row. While you edit REPEAT EVERY, the dial changes the value. Dial click REPEAT EVERY: starts or ends editing. AFTER SEND: changes the value. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

The device saves the memories when you leave the settings screen.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu lists every screen. Each row shows a number, the screen name, and what the screen holds.

To open the menu, press F4 (MENU) on the KEYER screen. Most other screens return to the menu with F4 (BACK).

Row Opens Page 01 KEYER The main screen: speed, tone, volume, timing tape and decode. Keyer 02 TIMING A zoomed timing tape and histograms of your keying. Timing 03 RECEIVE The Koch drill. F2 on that screen moves to the other drills and the ragchew. Receive drills 04 POTA Activate a park and work a pileup. Activate a park or summit 05 SOTA Activate a summit and work a pileup. Activate a park or summit 06 HUNT Hunt activators on parks and summits. Hunt 07 LETTERS Your accuracy for each character, and your mixups. Letters 08 PROGRESS Practice time and totals for recent sessions. Progress 09 SETTINGS Every setting. Settings 10 SYSTEM Version, hardware checks and battery. System 11 RADIO The decoder board of the Pro model. This row shows only when DECODER BOARD is ON. Radio

The header shows your callsign.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the KEYER tab. F2, F3 Nothing. F4 (BACK) Opens the KEYER screen. Dial turn Moves the selection up or down. Dial click Opens the selected screen. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
The PROGRESS screen shows your practice over recent sessions. A session is one time the device is on, from turn on to turn off. The device has no clock, so sessions take the place of days.

Open 08 PROGRESS in the menu. The header shows how many sessions the device keeps, such as 12 SESSIONS.

The device keeps the last 32 sessions. A session starts to count at the first thing you do, so a turn on with no practice does not take a place. When all 32 places are full, a new session replaces the oldest.

docs.title: What counts
docs.text: Column What it counts TIME Time while you key, on any screen. Time between two key presses counts when the gap is 60 seconds or less. SENT Characters you sent on the key, on any screen. COPY Percent right in receive drills and ragchew quizzes. QSOS QSOs you logged when you activate or hunt.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
The chart shows the last 14 sessions, the newest at the right. NOW marks the session in progress.

  • A filled bar shows the minutes of practice in that session.
  • A hollow square shows the COPY percent in that session. A session with no receive practice has no square.

The scale at the left shows the most minutes in the chart, 10 minutes or more.

The table under the chart has two rows:

  • NOW: this session. - means nothing counted yet.
  • LAST n: all the sessions the device keeps, added together.

Time shows as minutes, such as 25M, or as hours and minutes, such as 1H05. - in COPY means no receive practice.

Before your first session, the chart says NOTHING YET: START KEYING.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1, F3 Nothing. F2 (LTRS) Opens Letters. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Radio
docs.text:
The Pro model has a decoder board that listens to the audio of a radio. The RADIO screen shows the Morse code the board hears, as text.

No one has tried PocketCW on a Pro model yet. This screen follows the vendor firmware, but it is not tested on a board.

docs.title: Turn the decoder board on
docs.text:
1. Open the settings, and go to the RECV tab. See Settings.
  2. Set DECODER BOARD to ON. The device powers the decoder board.
  3. The menu now shows row 11 RADIO. Open it.

On a model without a decoder board, keep DECODER BOARD OFF. The setting is OFF by default.

Connect the radio's audio to the AUX1 port of the decoder board. Headphones or a powered speaker go in AUX2. The VOLUME setting also sets the volume of AUX2.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
The top line shows the state of the board:

Item Meaning BOARD OK or NO REPLY BOARD OK: the board announced itself after it got power. NO REPLY: the board did not announce itself yet. FIL n The filter setting of the board, 0 to 2. NR n The noise reduction level of the board, 0 to 6. nnWPM The speed of the Morse code the device hears. Two dashes stand in for the number before the first speed reading. ERR n Data errors on the link to the board. This item shows only after an error.

Under the top line, nine lines show the text the device decodes.

The device decodes only while the RADIO screen is open. Each time you open the screen, the decoder starts at 20 WPM and then follows the speed it hears, from 5 to 60 WPM. The text stays when you leave the screen.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the RECV tab. F4 (BACK) there returns to this screen. F2 (FILT) Changes the filter setting of the board: 0, 1, 2, then 0 again. F3 (NR) Changes the noise reduction level of the board: 0 to 6, then 0 again. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Clears the text. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Ragchew
docs.text:
In a ragchew, two stations hold a full QSO for you to copy. One station calls CQ, the other answers, and they trade signal reports, names, cities (QTH), rigs, antennas and weather (WX). Then they sign off with 73. After 8 overs, two new stations start a new QSO.

Open the ragchew from the receive drills: press F2 (KIND) on the CALLS drill. There are two kinds:

Kind What you do CHEW Listen. The text of each over shows after the over ends. QUIZ After an over, answer a question about it. The device scores your answer like a receive drill.

The stations send at CHAR SPEED, with FARNSWORTH spacing when you set it. With FIST set to HUMAN, each station keys with its own small timing errors. The two stations send at slightly different pitches. See Settings.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text: The screen shows each over in a list: the sender's callsign at the left of the first line, then the text. The two stations show in two colors. Text that you have not been shown yet shows as a row of dashes.

docs.title: CHEW
docs.text:
CHEW SHOWS on the RECV tab sets when text shows:

  • WHOLE OVER: each over shows after it ends.
  • EACH LINE: each line shows after it ends.

The footer repeats this choice.

docs.title: QUIZ
docs.text:
After an over that holds a fact, the screen asks one question, such as:

SENDER'S CALL?, RST?, NAME?, QTH CITY?, RIG?, POWER IN WATTS?, ANTENNA?, WX? or TEMPERATURE?

  1. The status shows YOUR TURN. Start to key the answer within 10 seconds.
  2. While you key, the status shows PAUSE ENDS: when you stop keying for three word gaps, your answer ends.
  3. The device shows the answer as sent, your copy with each character marked, and the score. The text of the over shows too. After 2.5 seconds the next over plays.

If you do not start to key within 10 seconds, the answer counts as missed. To hear the over again, key ? alone as your answer. The sign off overs have no question.

The footer shows your score for this session.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control Action F1 (SET) Pauses and opens the settings at the RECV tab. F4 (BACK) there returns, and the current over plays again at the new settings. F2 (KIND) CHEW: starts QUIZ. QUIZ: starts the KOCH drill. F3 (STOP or GO) Pauses, or starts again from the start of the current over. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key QUIZ: keys your answer. CHEW: nothing more.

Quiz scores also go to Letters and Progress.

docs.title: Receive drills
docs.text:
In a receive drill, the device sends a group of characters, and you key back what you copied. The device then shows the group with each character marked right or wrong.

To start, open 03 RECEIVE in the menu. The Koch drill starts. F2 (KIND) moves to the next drill:

KOCH, WORDS, CALLS, then the ragchew CHEW and QUIZ, then KOCH again.

Drill What the device sends KOCH Groups of 5 characters from the Koch characters of your level. WORDS One common word or abbreviation heard on the air, such as QTH, 5NN or <BK>. CALLS One US callsign.

The device sends at CHAR SPEED, with FARNSWORTH spacing when you set it. See the RECV tab in Settings. The header shows the drill and the speed, such as 20WPM, or 20/10WPM with Farnsworth spacing.

docs.title: How a drill runs
docs.text:
1. The device sends a group. The status shows LISTEN.
  2. The status shows YOUR TURN. Start to key what you copied within 5 seconds. You can also start while the group still plays.
  3. While you key, the status shows PAUSE ENDS: when you stop keying for three word gaps, your copy ends.
  4. The device scores your copy and shows it in the list. The next group starts after about 1 second.

If you do not start to key within 5 seconds, the group counts as missed.

To hear the group again, key ? alone as your copy.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
• The top line: in KOCH, your level and your progress to the next level, such as LEVEL 5 80% OF 30 NEED 90% OF 50.
  • The character set, each character in the color of how well you copy it. Green: you know it. Amber: not enough tries to tell. Red, inverted: weak. Gray: not sent yet. KOCH shows the characters of your level, and a line marks the newest one. WORDS and CALLS show all 44 characters.
  • The list of recent groups. Each row shows the group that was sent, then your copy with each character marked: green for right, red and inverted for wrong, _ for missed. The score shows at the right, such as 4/5.
  • Your copy as you key it, with the status at the right.
  • The footer: your score for this session, such as SESSION 85% 120 CHARS.

docs.title: The Koch method
docs.text:
The KOCH drill starts at level 2, with K and M. You move up one level when you copy at least 90 % right over 50 characters. Each level adds the next character in this order:

K M U R E S N A P T L W I . J Z = F O Y , V G 5 / Q 9 2 H 3 8 B ? 4 7 C 1 D 6 0 X <AR> <SK> <KN>

The score counts extra characters you key as errors, the same as missed ones. After 50 characters below 90 %, the count starts again. When you move up, the status line shows the new character, such as LEVEL UP: ADDED U.

The drill picks weak characters more often, and the newest character twice as often.

The device keeps your level and your progress toward the next level while you use other screens. The level stays after you turn the device off.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control Action F1 (SET) Pauses the drill and opens the settings at the RECV tab. F4 (BACK) there returns, and the next group plays at the new settings. F2 (KIND) Starts the next drill. F3 (STOP or GO) Pauses the drill, or starts it again. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu. Dial turn KOCH only: sets your level, 2 to 44. A new level starts its progress count from zero. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Keys your copy.

Your scores also go to Letters and Progress.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: All settings are on one screen with seven tabs: KEYER, SOUND, RECV, QSO, THEME, CALL and MEM. The device saves the settings 2 seconds after your last change.

docs.title: Open the settings
docs.text:
From Press Opens at tab Menu, row 09 SETTINGS Dial click KEYER Menu, KEYER, TIMING F1 (SET) KEYER Receive drills, ragchew, LETTERS, RADIO F1 (SET) RECV POTA, SOTA, HUNT F1 (SET) QSO SYSTEM F1 (SET) THEME

F4 (BACK) leaves the settings and returns to the screen you came from. A drill or a QSO you paused continues. From row 09 of the menu, F4 (BACK) returns to the menu.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
These controls work on the KEYER, SOUND, RECV, QSO and THEME tabs. The CALL and MEM tabs have their own controls.

Control Action F1 (TAB) Opens the next tab. After MEM, KEYER opens again. F2 (-) Changes the value of the selected row down one step. F3 (+) Changes the value of the selected row up one step. F4 (BACK) Leaves the settings. Dial turn Selects another row. While you edit, changes the value. Dial click Starts or ends editing the selected row. While you edit, the value shows as < value >. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

Numbers stop at their lowest and highest values. A choice of words goes around: after the last value, the first value comes again.

docs.title: KEYER tab
docs.text: Row Values Default What it sets MODE IAMBIC A, IAMBIC B, STRAIGHT IAMBIC B Your key type. See Keys and jacks. PADDLES NORMAL, REVERSED NORMAL NORMAL: dots on the tip contact. REVERSED: dots on the ring contact. STRAIGHT mode ignores this row. SPEED 5 to 60 WPM 20 WPM Your sending speed. KEY OUT ON, OFF ON Whether the func jack keys. OUT TYPE STRAIGHT, PADDLE STRAIGHT STRAIGHT: one line keys, for a radio's straight key input. PADDLE: two lines follow your contacts, for the radio's own keyer. OUT LINES TIP KEYS, RING KEYS (STRAIGHT); DIT ON TIP, DIT ON RING (PADDLE) TIP KEYS or DIT ON TIP Which lines of the func jack key. USB OUT OFF, TEXT, VBAND OFF What the USB port sends a computer. TEXT types what you key. VBAND sends your keying to VBand. See USB keyboard.

docs.title: SOUND tab
docs.text:
Row Values Default What it sets TONE 300 to 1200 Hz, in steps of 10 Hz 700 Hz The pitch of your sidetone. Other stations send at pitches near it. VOLUME 0 to 44 23 0 is off. Each step is 1.5 dB. WAVE SINE, SQUARE SINE SINE is a pure tone. SQUARE is a buzzier tone with soft edges. NOISE OFF, 1 to 10 OFF Band noise under the stations you hear. FADING OFF, 1 to 10 OFF How deep the stations you hear fade in and out.

The tab says NOISE AND FADING: DRILLS, QSO, HUNT: noise and fading play in the receive drills, the ragchew, and on the POTA, SOTA and HUNT screens. While the SOUND tab is open, the band noise plays, so you hear the level you set.

docs.title: RECV tab
docs.text:
Row Values Default What it sets CHAR SPEED MATCH, 5 to 40 WPM MATCH The speed of each character the device sends you. MATCH uses your keyer SPEED. FARNSWORTH OFF, 5 to 40 WPM OFF Longer gaps between characters and words, so the text comes at this slower overall speed. It never goes above CHAR SPEED. CHEW SHOWS WHOLE OVER, EACH LINE WHOLE OVER When the ragchew CHEW shows its text. DECODER BOARD ON, OFF OFF ON: the device powers the decoder board of the Pro model, and the menu shows row 11 RADIO. See Radio.

The tab says SPEED OF WHAT YOU HEAR: BOTS, DRILLS: CHAR SPEED and FARNSWORTH set the speed of every station the device sends you.

docs.title: QSO tab
docs.text:
Row Values Default What it sets CHAR SPEED MATCH, 5 to 40 WPM MATCH The same setting as CHAR SPEED on the RECV tab. FARNSWORTH OFF, 5 to 40 WPM OFF The same setting as FARNSWORTH on the RECV tab. PILEUP OFF, TAKE TURNS, OVERLAP TAKE TURNS How the hunters call when you activate. FIST HUMAN, CLEAN HUMAN HUMAN: each station keys with small timing errors. CLEAN: exact timing. SPEED SPREAD ON, OFF ON ON: each hunter or activator sends up to 5 WPM faster or slower than CHAR SPEED.

The tab says SAME SPEEDS AS THE RECV TAB.

docs.title: THEME tab
docs.text:
Row Values Default What it sets STYLE HAZARD, HUD, BLOCK HAZARD The shapes of the screen: the frame, the header, the button labels and the selection. PALETTE 16 palettes ORANGE The colors of the screen and of the boot screen. BRIGHTNESS 10 % to 100 %, in steps of 10 % 100 % The brightness of the screen.

The palettes are ORANGE, CYAN, AMBER, LIME, DAILY, and the pride flags RAINBOW, TRANS, BI, LESBIAN, PAN, NONBIN, ACE, ARO, FLUID, AGENDER and QUEER. DAILY shows a different flag each time you turn the device on, and the tab says A NEW FLAG EACH BOOT. Under the rows, a swatch shows the colors of each palette, with a frame around the selected one.

The colors that grade your timing are the same in every palette: green, amber and red.

docs.title: CALL tab
docs.text:
The CALL tab shows your callsign in large letters. The QSO and hunt screens use it, and the boot screen draws it. The default is N0CALL, a placeholder callsign.

Key your callsign on the key. Each character you key goes at the end. A callsign holds up to 10 characters: letters, digits and /. The device ignores other characters.

Control Action F1 (TAB) Opens the next tab. F2 (DEL) Deletes the last character. F3 (CLR) Deletes the whole callsign. F4 (BACK) Leaves the settings. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Adds characters to your callsign.

docs.title: MEM tab
docs.text: The MEM tab holds your four memories. See Memories.

docs.title: Status messages
docs.text: The status line at the bottom of the screen shows short messages. In this list, n is a number and X is a character.

docs.title: Power and battery
docs.text:
Message Meaning RELEASE TO POWER OFF You held the dial for 1.5 seconds. Let go of the dial to turn the device off. BATTERY LOW: PLUG IN USB The battery is below 3.4 V. Connect USB power to charge it. BATTERY EMPTY: POWERING OFF The battery is empty. After 2 seconds the device saves everything and turns off.

See System.

docs.title: Saves
docs.text:
Each of these messages means a write to the memory chip failed. The device keeps the values while it is on, but they can be lost when it turns off.

Message What was not saved SETTINGS NOT SAVED Your settings. MEMORIES NOT SAVED Your memories. LETTER STATS NOT SAVED Your letter statistics and Koch level. PROGRESS NOT SAVED This session in Progress. BATTERY CALIBRATION NOT SAVED The full point of the battery gauge.

When a save fails at power off, the device waits 3 seconds before it turns off, so you can read the message. If these messages come again and again, look at the EEPROM row on the System screen.

docs.title: Key and hardware
docs.text: Message Meaning DIT STUCK ON: CHECK PLUG A contact of the key jack stayed closed too long, and stopped keying until it opens. The message names DIT, DAH, TIP or RNG. See Keys and jacks. CODEC DID NOT ANSWER The audio chip did not take a new volume. n INPUTS LOST Button presses, key changes or decoded characters came faster than the screen could handle them, and the device lost n of them. n USB KEYS LOST The device lost n characters or key changes on their way to the computer. See USB keyboard.

docs.title: Memories
docs.text:
These messages show on the KEYER screen. See Memories.

Message Meaning CLICK CLOSES The memory row is open. A dial click closes it. LIT M REPEATS CLICK CLOSES The memory row is open, and a lit label marks a memory that repeats. SENDING Mn KEY TO STOP Memory n is sending. Touch your key to stop it. Mn AGAIN IN nS KEY TO STOP Memory n repeats after the time shown. Mn TONE ONLY: OUT IS PADDLE Memory n plays as a tone and does not key the func jack, because OUT TYPE is PADDLE. Mn IS EMPTY (SETTINGS, MEM) Memory n holds no message. Key one in on the MEM tab of the settings. MEMORY FULL On the MEM tab: the memory has no room for the last character you keyed. A memory holds up to 48 characters, and a prosign such as <AR> takes 4.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text: Message Meaning LEVEL UP: ADDED X You moved up a Koch level, and the drill now sends character X too. See Receive drills. CLR AGAIN TO ERASE STATS On the LETTERS screen: press F2 (CLR) again to erase your letter statistics. See Letters.

docs.title: The red error screen
docs.text: If PocketCW finds an error it cannot continue from, the screen turns dark red and shows what went wrong. The func jack and the LED turn off, so a radio does not stay keyed. Click the dial to turn the device off. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Go back to the stock firmware
docs.text: This page puts the original HamCube firmware, version V5.03, back on the device. PocketCW does not include the HamCube files. The install script downloads them from a separate source.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Board 2.64 has a different sound chip (an ES8388). The published stock versions, V5.03 and the beta V5.03.13, have no setup for that chip, so the speaker is silent under them. At least one board 2.64 came from the factory with V5.03.15, a version HamCube has not published, and its sound worked. If your device came with a stock version newer than V5.03.13, you cannot get that version back after you install PocketCW.

Boards from 2.63 have an IPS screen. Stock V5.03 has no setup for the IPS screen, so it shows that screen on its side, in strips. The beta version V5.03.13 sets up the IPS screen, but only on boards that read as version 2.63. No published stock version fully supports board 2.64.

The SYSTEM screen of PocketCW shows your board version on the BOARD row.

Stock firmware keeps its settings in a different part of the memory chip than PocketCW. If you install PocketCW again later, it finds its settings again.

docs.title: The two stock files
docs.text:
The stock firmware is two files from HamCube's V5.03 upgrade package:

  • F0000C0.bin holds the images of the stock screens. The stock firmware draws its screens from the device's image memory, and an older V5.02 copy of this file scrambles the stock screen. The images stay in the image memory, so a device needs this file only once. PocketCW never reads the image memory, so PocketCW works with any version of this file.
  • A000014.bin is the stock firmware.

HamCube says to install F0000C0.bin before A000014.bin.

PocketCW does not include these files. The install script downloads them from github.com/admvip/CW-Pokemon-Infomation, and checks that each one matches the V5.03 file.

docs.title: Windows and Linux
docs.text:
1. Download F0000C0.bin and A000014.bin from the "CW Pokemon V5.03 Upgrade package" folder of the HamCube files. If the device has had the V5.03 images installed before, you need only A000014.bin.
  2. Copy F0000C0.bin to the update drive, as in Install.
  3. Put the device in update mode again, and copy A000014.bin the same way.
  4. Unplug the device, then click the dial to turn it on.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
Start the script as in Start the script, with this line in place of the PocketCW line:

curl -fsSL https://kvmet.github.io/k5mme_pocketcw/install.sh | sh -s stock

Then:

  1. The script asks whether the device has had the V5.03 images installed before. If you are not sure, press Return: the script then installs the images first.
  2. Follow the steps the script prints. With the images, the script installs two files, and you put the device in update mode once for each file.
  3. When the script says "Finished", unplug the device, then click the dial to turn it on.

To install PocketCW again, follow Install. PocketCW needs no F file.

docs.title: The beta for board 2.63
docs.text:
On a board 2.63, you can use the beta V5.03.13 in place of the V5.03 A000014.bin. The install script does not download the beta.

  1. Install the stock firmware with the steps above, so the device has the V5.03 images.
  2. In the HamCube files, open the folder "CW Pokemon Beta Upgrade package", download V5.03.13Beta.zip, and unzip it. It holds only A000014.bin.
  3. Copy that A000014.bin to the update drive, as in Install. On a Mac, use the install tool below in place of a copy.

On a Mac, download the PocketCW install tool in Terminal, and make it a program you can run:

curl -fsSLo ~/Downloads/pocketcw-flash https://github.com/kvmet/k5mme_pocketcw/releases/latest/download/pocketcw-flash

chmod +x ~/Downloads/pocketcw-flash

Then run the tool on the beta file, and follow the steps it prints. Replace the path with the place of your file:

~/Downloads/pocketcw-flash ~/Downloads/V5.03.13Beta/A000014.bin

docs.title: System
docs.text:
The SYSTEM screen shows the firmware version, the results of the startup checks, and the battery. Open 10 SYSTEM in the menu.

A value in red shows a problem.

docs.title: Rows
docs.text:
Row Example What it shows FIRMWARE v0.2.0 The PocketCW version. BOARD 2.64 IPS AUTO The board version, the kind of screen, and how the device picked the kind of screen. See below. MCU AT32F403A 256K The processor and its flash memory size. CLOCK 72 MHZ XTAL The processor speed and its clock source. XTAL is the crystal. HICK, in red, is the less exact internal clock. CODEC ES8388 OK The audio chip and whether it answered. NONE FOUND means no audio chip answered. EEPROM 24C16 OK The memory chip that holds your settings and statistics. With FAIL, the device cannot save. BATTERY 3.95V 70% 2443 The battery voltage, the charge in percent, and the raw reading. With USB power, it shows USB and the voltage. Red when the battery is low. SUPPLY 3.29V The voltage the processor runs on. UPTIME 0:12:05 Hours, minutes and seconds since the device turned on. BOOTS 57 How many times PocketCW started.

ADC FAIL in BATTERY and SUPPLY means the device could not read the voltages.

Under the rows, two small lines show what the screen answered on pins B4 and B5 when the device asked for its ID (FLOAT means no answer), and the unique ID of the processor. These help when you report a problem.

docs.title: How the device picks the kind of screen
docs.text:
BOARD shows The kind of screen comes from AUTO The board version. ID The ID the screen gave. SET Your choice: you held F2 when you turned the device on. NOSAVE, in red You held F2 when you turned the device on, but the device could not save the choice.

To change the kind of screen, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Battery
docs.text:
The battery icon at the right end of the header shows the charge:

Icon Meaning Plus sign USB power. 1 to 4 bars The charge, in quarters. Red outline, no bars The battery is low.

The device learns where full charge reads on your battery. A battery gauge reads a little differently on each board. The device takes a new full point when the battery reads higher than before, after 2 minutes without USB power. The full point stays within 3 % of the design value. The device saves the full point.

When the battery goes below 3.4 V, the status line says BATTERY LOW: PLUG IN USB. When the battery stays below 3.2 V, or the supply below 3.1 V, for 10 seconds, the status line says BATTERY EMPTY: POWERING OFF. After 2 seconds, the device saves everything and turns off.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the THEME tab. F4 (BACK) there returns to this screen. F2, F3 Nothing. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Timing
docs.text:
The TIMING screen gives a close look at your keying. The header shows TIMING, the keyer mode and your speed.

The screen measures every mark and gap against the dot length the decoder uses: the dot length of your set speed in the iambic modes, or of the speed you actually send in STRAIGHT mode. It grades each mark and gap as good, off or bad. See Timing grades.

docs.title: Zoomed tape
docs.text:
The tape draws time from left to right, 8 pixels per dot length.

  • The SET row shows brackets around the ideal length of each mark.
  • The YOU row shows each mark you sent, in the color and shape of its grade. A good mark is solid, an off mark has a stripe through it, and a bad mark is an outline.
  • Over each mark, a number shows its error in percent: +10 is 10 % long, -10 is 10 % short.
  • Under the marks, each decoded character shows, and each gap between characters or words shows its length in units.
  • A gap inside a character that is off or bad gets an underline in its grade.

docs.title: Histograms
docs.text:
Histogram Range Dotted lines at MARKS 0 to 4 units 1 (dot) and 3 (dash) GAPS 0 to 8 units 1 (inside a character), 3 (between characters) and 7 (between words)

Each bar counts the marks or gaps of that length, in the color of the grade a mark or gap of that length gets.

docs.title: Averages
docs.text:
Line What it shows DIT Average dot length and its standard deviation (SD) in milliseconds, then RATIO: average dash over average dot. The ideal ratio is 3. DAH Average dash length and its standard deviation in milliseconds, then the speed your timing works out to. GAP, CHR, WRD Average gap inside characters, between characters and between words, in units.

The statistics collect your keying on every screen since the device was turned on, or since you last pressed F2 (CLR). The KEYER screen shows the same statistics.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the KEYER tab. F2 (CLR) Clears the statistics and the tape. F3 Nothing. F4 (BACK) Opens the KEYER screen. Dial turn Nothing. Dial click Nothing. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Draws on the tape and adds to the statistics.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists install problems first, then problems on the device.

docs.title: Install messages
docs.text: These messages come from the macOS install tool. When it finds a problem, it prints Problem: and one of these messages, then waits. Do what the message says, press Return, and follow the steps the tool prints again.

docs.title: "could not download"
docs.text: The script could not reach GitHub. Check that the Mac is connected to the internet, and run the line from Start the script again.

docs.title: "the update drive is mounted"
docs.text: The device was in update mode before the script started, so macOS opened its drive. Eject the drive in Finder. Its name is POKEMON-2 or HAM MODULE. Unplug the device, and press Return.

docs.title: "no update drive appeared in 180 seconds"
docs.text:
The Mac did not find the device in update mode. Check these two things:

  • The device showed the firmware update screen before you plugged it in. See Update mode.
  • The cable carries data. Try another cable or another USB port.

Then press Return.

docs.title: "macOS did not allow writing to the device"
docs.text: The password box was closed with Cancel. Press Return, and type your Mac login password when macOS asks. If the box shakes, the password was wrong: type it again.

docs.title: "the device status is ..., not Ready"
docs.text: The update drive is not ready to take a file. Hold F4, which resets the drive, then press Return. If the message comes back, unplug the device and press Return.

docs.title: "the drive already holds a file"
docs.text: macOS wrote something to the drive before the install tool could stop it. Hold F4 to reset the drive, then press Return.

docs.title: "the status stayed Ready for 10 s; the device did not take the file"
docs.text: The write did not finish. Press Return to install again.

docs.title: "the device dropped off USB before showing Success"
docs.text: The tool cannot tell whether the write finished. Press Return to install again.

docs.title: "the device status is ..., not Success"
docs.text: The device reported a problem with the file. Press Return to install again. If the message comes back, report it on the issue tracker with the status the message shows.

docs.title: "is not the V5.03 file this script expects"
docs.text: The script restores the stock firmware only from the exact V5.03 files. The downloaded file is different, so the script stopped before it changed anything. Report it on the issue tracker.

docs.title: The device shows the update screen when you only want to use it
docs.text:
If the battery is full and the device is plugged into USB, it sometimes starts in update mode. Unplug USB and click the dial to turn it on.

If the device starts in update mode every time, even unplugged, the last install did not finish. Install again.

docs.title: The screen is turned on its side, or shows the picture in strips
docs.text:
Boards use one of two kinds of screen, and the firmware cannot always tell which one it has. To switch to the other kind:

  1. Hold the dial down for about 2 seconds. The device turns off, even though you cannot read the screen.
  2. Hold F2 down. F2 is the second button from the top.
  3. While you hold F2, click the dial to turn the device on.
  4. Let go of F2 when the screen shows a picture.

The device remembers the choice. To switch back, do the same steps again.

docs.title: The device does not start after an install
docs.text: Run the install again from step 1. The install never changes the bootloader, so update mode always works.

docs.title: A red screen with an error
docs.text: The firmware stopped on an error it cannot recover from. Click the dial to turn the device off. Then turn it on again. If the error comes back, copy the text on the screen into a report on the issue tracker.

docs.title: No sound
docs.text: Check the volume: the VOL value on the KEYER screen, or VOLUME on the SOUND tab of the settings. At 0 the sound is off. A plug in the headphone jack turns the speaker off.

docs.title: A message on the bottom line of the screen
docs.text: See Status messages.

docs.title: USB keyboard
docs.text:
The device can show up on a computer, phone or tablet as a USB keyboard. Set USB OUT on the KEYER tab of the settings.

USB OUT What the computer gets OFF Nothing. The USB port only charges the battery. This is the default. TEXT Each character you key, typed as text. VBAND Your keying as the Ctrl keys, for VBand.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. Turn the device on.
  2. Plug the USB cable into the device and the computer.

The computer finds a keyboard named PocketCW. It needs no driver. The first time, macOS can open its Keyboard Setup Assistant. Close it.

If the device is plugged into USB when you turn it on, it can start in update mode. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: TEXT
docs.text:
The device types each character that the decoder reads from your key. Use it with any program that takes typed text, such as a copy trainer or a text editor.

  • A character types after the gap that ends it, as it shows on the screen.
  • A word gap types one space.
  • Letters type in lowercase.
  • A pattern that is not a character types *. A prosign types between angle brackets, such as <AR>, as on the screen.
  • It works on every screen, with every key type.

docs.title: Keyboard layout
docs.text:
The device sends the keys of a US keyboard, and the computer turns each key into a character with its own layout setting.

  • With a US layout, every character types correctly.
  • With another layout, letters and digits are mostly correct, but punctuation such as /, ?, @ and " can type other characters. Some layouts also exchange Y and Z.

For exact text, set the computer's keyboard layout to US.

docs.title: Phones and tablets
docs.text: While a USB keyboard is connected, an iPhone or iPad hides its on-screen keyboard. To charge the device from a phone or tablet, set USB OUT to OFF.

docs.title: VBAND
docs.text:
VBAND sends your keying the way the VBand USB adapter does. In VBand, set the key type to match MODE on the KEYER tab.

MODE The device sends Set VBand to IAMBIC A, IAMBIC B The dot lever holds Left Ctrl, and the dash lever holds Right Ctrl. PADDLES sets which lever is which. An iambic paddle. VBand times the elements with its own keyer. STRAIGHT Left Ctrl, held while the device keys. This works for a straight key and a sideswiper. A straight key.

docs.title: Status message
docs.text: n USB KEYS LOST means the device lost n characters or key changes on their way to the computer. See Status messages.
